definition_zh: 温室效应；大气保温效应；温室内的升温效应
definition_en: the warming of a planet's surface caused by gases in its atmosphere that let sunlight in but hold back outgoing heat
core_image: 一层透明的玻璃罩住菜畦，阳光照进来，热气却出不去
scene: 玻璃花房里阳光直射进来，地面热气被挡在玻璃内侧，温度计一路上升。 The greenhouse effect kept the flower house warm long after the sun had gone behind the hill.
sceneCN: 这里指「透明覆盖物让阳光进入、又拦住热量外散所造成的升温」（第 1 个义项：大气或透光层截留长波辐射、使表面升温的机制）；句意为太阳落到山后很久，温室效应仍让花房保持温暖。图中可辨识物件：玻璃屋顶、菜畦、温度计、山影。

senses.title: Heat held by an atmosphere
senses.titleCN: 大气截留热量所造成的升温
senses.definition: the process by which gases in a planet's atmosphere let short-wave sunlight pass but absorb and return long-wave heat
senses.definitionCN: 行星大气中的气体让短波阳光通过、却吸收并回送长波热量的过程
senses.example: The greenhouse effect kept the flower house warm long after the sun had gone behind the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳落到山后很久，温室效应仍让花房保持温暖。
senses.why: The name borrows the glass house: glass admits light and holds the warmth inside, and the atmosphere does the same with certain gases.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字借自玻璃温室：玻璃让光进入又把热留在里面，大气凭借某些气体也做同样的事。

senses.title: The human strengthening of that process
senses.titleCN: 人为排放导致的温室效应增强
senses.definition: the added warming produced when human emissions raise the concentration of heat-trapping gases
senses.definitionCN: 人类排放提高截热气体浓度后所增加的变暖
senses.example: The enhanced greenhouse effect is what the treaty tries to limit.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约想要限制的正是增强的温室效应。
senses.why: Once the natural mechanism was understood, the same phrase was used for the human addition, usually marked by the word enhanced.
senses.whyCN: 自然机制被理解之后，同一短语便用于人为附加的部分，通常加上「增强的」一词来标记。

senses.title: The literal warming inside a glasshouse
senses.titleCN: 玻璃温室内实际的升温现象
senses.definition: the rise in temperature inside a glass building used for plants, caused by trapped solar heat
senses.definitionCN: 用于栽培植物的玻璃建筑内部因太阳能被截留而升温
senses.example: The greenhouse effect in the old glasshouse was strong enough to ripen figs.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧玻璃房里的温室效应足以让无花果成熟。
senses.why: This is the original observation, and the scientific term preserves it as a literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的观察，科学术语把它保留为一个字面义项。

senses.title: The same mechanism on other planets
senses.titleCN: 其他行星大气上的同类机制
senses.definition: the warming of another planet's surface by its own atmospheric gases
senses.definitionCN: 其他行星表面因其自身大气气体而升温
senses.example: Venus shows how far a greenhouse effect can go.
senses.exampleCN: 金星展示了温室效应能走到多远。
senses.why: Planetary science generalized the earthbound term, since the physics depends on gases and pressure rather than on glass.
senses.whyCN: 行星科学把这个地球上的术语一般化，因为其中的物理取决于气体与气压，而非玻璃。

senses.title: The radiation budget in plain terms
senses.definition: the imbalance in which incoming short-wave radiation exceeds outgoing long-wave radiation at the surface
senses.definitionCN: 地表接收的短波辐射多于向外散失的长波辐射这一不平衡
senses.example: The greenhouse effect is a budget statement, not a blanket.
senses.exampleCN: 温室效应是一笔收支账，而不是一条毯子。
senses.why: Physicists restated the everyday image as a balance of incoming and outgoing radiation, and the phrase carried over.
senses.whyCN: 物理学家把日常意象改写为进出辐射的收支，并沿用了这个短语。

senses.title: A trapped and amplified effect
senses.titleCN: 比喻：封闭系统内被放大的效应
senses.definition: any situation in which a closed setting traps something and multiplies its effect
senses.definitionCN: 任何封闭环境把某物截住并放大其作用的局面
senses.example: Online outrage has its own greenhouse effect: heat stays and compounds.
senses.exampleCN: 网络上的愤怒自有其温室效应：热度留存并不断叠加。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps two parts of the original: a boundary that holds, and a build-up that follows from holding.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了原义的两部分：一道拦住的边界，以及因拦住而产生的累积。

senses.title: A shorthand in climate policy
senses.titleCN: 气候政策话语中的简称
senses.definition: a short way of naming the atmospheric mechanism in public and policy discussion
senses.definitionCN: 在公共与政策讨论中称呼大气机制的简便说法
senses.example: The briefing put the greenhouse effect before every other item.
senses.exampleCN: 简报把温室效应排在所有议题之前。
senses.why: Policy needed a compact label that a general audience already knew, so the technical phrase became a shorthand.
senses.whyCN: 政策需要一个公众已经知道的简短标签，于是这个技术短语成了简称。

senses.title: A self-reinforcing warming loop
senses.titleCN: 比喻：使状况不断升温的循环
senses.definition: a feedback loop in which warming causes changes that cause still more warming
senses.definitionCN: 变暖引起变化、变化又引起更多变暖的反馈循环
senses.example: Melting ice creates a greenhouse effect of its own by darkening the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 冰层融化使地面变暗，从而造出它自己的温室效应。
senses.why: The feedback sense pushes the image further: the trapped heat now changes the container so that it traps more.
senses.whyCN: 反馈义把意象再推一步：被截住的热改变了容器，使它截住更多。

intro.en: Greenhouse effect is a modern English compound of greenhouse, a glass building for plants, and effect from Latin effectus 'accomplishment'. The phrase was formed in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: greenhouse effect 是近代英语复合词，由 greenhouse（栽培植物的玻璃建筑）与来自拉丁 effectus「完成、结果」的 effect 构成。这个短语成形于十九世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greenhouse is an English compound of green 'growing, verdant' and house, naming a glass building where plants are kept warm out of season.
items.cn: greenhouse 是英语复合词，由 green「青绿的、生长的」与 house 构成，指让植物在不当季时也保持温暖的玻璃建筑。

items.en: Effectus 'a doing, accomplishment' came from efficere 'to work out', itself ex- 'out' plus facere 'to do, make'. The noun is the source of English effect.
items.cn: effectus「做成、完成」来自 efficere「做出」，后者由 ex-「向外」加 facere「做、造」构成。这个名词是英语 effect 的来源。

items.en: In the 1820s Fourier described how the atmosphere keeps a planet warmer than its distance from the sun would allow; the glass-house comparison followed and gave the phenomenon its name.
items.cn: 十九世纪二十年代，傅里叶描述了大气如何使行星比按日距推算的更暖；随后出现的玻璃房类比给了这一现象名字。

items.en: The phrase greenhouse effect was current in English by the later nineteenth century and was used alongside the French phrase effet de serre.
items.cn: 到十九世纪后期，greenhouse effect 这一短语已在英语中通行，并与法语 effet de serre 并用。

items.en: Twentieth-century climatology split the natural mechanism from the human enhancement, and both readings now sit inside one phrase.
items.cn: 二十世纪的气候学把自然机制与人为增强分开，而两种读法如今都容在同一个短语里。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the exact first appearance of the English phrase is not firmly dated, though the underlying idea is securely traced to the 1820s. No part of the compound is doubtful in form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：这个英语短语的确切首见时间没有定论，但其背后的思想可确凿追溯到十九世纪二十年代。复合词本身的形态并无疑点。

note.en: Group one holds phrases built with greenhouse that look almost the same; group two holds the names of warming processes and quantities.
note.cn: 第一组是同样含 greenhouse、外形几乎相同的短语；第二组是各种变暖过程与相关量的名称。

entries.definition: A gas that traps heat; the effect is what such gases produce together, not the gas itself.
entries.definitionCN: 截住热量的气体；效应是这类气体共同造成的结果，而非气体本身。

entries.definition: The warming attributed to trapped heat, an observed result rather than the mechanism that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 归因于被截热量的变暖，是观测到的结果而非产生它的机制。

entries.definition: The glass structure that supplied the image; it names a place, not an atmospheric process.
entries.definitionCN: 提供这一意象的玻璃建筑；它指一处场所，而非大气过程。

entries.definition: An occasional synonym built on glasshouse; it never displaced the greenhouse form in scientific use.
entries.definitionCN: 偶尔使用的同义词，以 glasshouse 构词；在科学用法中从未取代 greenhouse 形式。

entries.definition: The measured rise in the earth's average temperature; it is the outcome that the greenhouse effect helps explain.
entries.definitionCN: 地球平均气温的实测上升；它是温室效应所解释的结果。

entries.definition: The change in the energy balance of the climate system, a quantitative measure rather than a named mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 气候系统能量平衡的改变，是定量指标而非一个有名字的机制。

entries.definition: Local warming over built-up ground; it shares the word effect but has nothing to do with atmospheric gases.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑密集地面上空的局地升温；与 effect 一词共享形式，但与大气气体无关。

entries.definition: Material that slows heat flow; the greenhouse effect works by radiation, not by blocking conduction.
entries.definitionCN: 减缓热流的材料；温室效应靠辐射起作用，而不是阻断传导。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The name is a comparison: glass admits light and refuses heat, and so does an atmosphere with certain gases.
normal.cn: 这个名字是一个比较：玻璃放光进来、不让热出去，含某些气体的大气亦然。

normal.en: Effect comes from efficere 'to work out', so the phrase says the atmosphere works something out.
normal.cn: effect 来自 efficere「做出」，因此这个短语是说大气「做出」了某个结果。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the readings: natural greenhouse effect, enhanced greenhouse effect, runaway greenhouse effect.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分各种读法：自然温室效应、增强的温室效应、失控的温室效应。

normal.en: The family includes greenhouse, greenhouse gas, greenhouse warming and the adjective effective.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 greenhouse、greenhouse gas、greenhouse warming 与形容词 effective。

normal.en: Venus is the standard example of the mechanism running to extremes.
normal.cn: 金星是该机制走到极端的标准例子。

abstract.en: Picture a car with all its windows shut on a sunny day.
abstract.cn: 想象晴天里车窗全部关着的汽车。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour that stays in one room and grows louder each time it is repeated.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻留在同一间屋里，每被重复一次就更响。

abstract.en: Picture a blanket that also warms the person who keeps adding layers.
abstract.cn: 想象一条毯子，也给不断加层的人升温。

examples.en: Without any greenhouse effect, the earth's surface would average well below freezing.
examples.cn: 若完全没有温室效应，地表平均温度会远低于冰点。

examples.en: Carbon dioxide strengthens the greenhouse effect by absorbing outgoing infrared radiation.
examples.cn: 二氧化碳吸收向外散出的红外辐射，从而加强温室效应。

examples.en: The students built a box model to show the greenhouse effect in miniature.
examples.cn: 学生们做了一个箱式模型，用缩小的方式演示温室效应。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「green（绿）+ house（房子）+ effect（效应）」——玻璃房里菜绿了、热也出不去了 → 温室效应

root: 英语复合词：greenhouse 由 green 与 house 构成，指栽培植物的玻璃房；effect 来自拉丁 effectus「做成、结果」，出自 efficere（ex- + facere）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one comparison: a transparent boundary lets light in and holds heat back, whether the boundary is glass, an atmosphere, another planet's air, a policy label or a closed room of anger.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个比较展开：一道透明边界让光进入、把热拦住，无论这道边界是玻璃、大气、别的行星的空气、一个政策标签，还是一间封闭的怒气之屋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sunlight enters a glass house, warmth stays inside, the thermometer climbs.
core.cn: 核心意象：阳光进入玻璃房，热量留在里面，温度计上升。

branches.en: MECHANISM: the atmosphere plays the part of glass in a radiation budget.
branches.cn: 机制：大气在辐射收支中扮演玻璃的角色。

branches.en: HUMAN READING: the same phrase names the added part and serves as a policy label.
branches.cn: 人为读法：同一短语指附加的部分，并充当政策标签。

branches.en: LITERAL HOUSE: the glass building is the original observation behind the term.
branches.cn: 字面的房子：玻璃建筑是这个术语背后的最初观察。

branches.en: OTHER WORLDS: the physics travels to any planet with an atmosphere.
branches.cn: 别的世界：这套物理适用于任何有大气层的行星。

branches.en: TRAPPED AND AMPLIFIED: a closed setting holds something until it compounds.
branches.cn: 被截留并放大：封闭环境把某物留住，直到它不断叠加。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two free English words, one Germanic and one Latin-derived, and both bring large families with them.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个自由的英语词构成，一个属日耳曼语来源，一个属拉丁来源，两者都带来大批同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere 'to do' yields effect, effective, efficient, factory and manufacture; greenhouse supplies greenhouse gas and greenhouse warming.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 facere「做」衍生 effect、effective、efficient、factory 与 manufacture；greenhouse 则构成 greenhouse gas 与 greenhouse warming。

senses.exampleCN: 典礼改在主礼堂举行。
senses.why: The Latin ending -orium names a place, so the word literally means the place for hearing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词尾 -orium 表示场所，所以这个词字面意思就是「听的场所」。

senses.title: The seating area of a theatre
senses.definition: the part of a theatre where the audience sits, as opposed to the stage
senses.definitionCN: 剧场中观众就座的部分，与舞台相对
senses.example: The auditorium was dark while the stage was lit.
senses.exampleCN: 舞台亮着灯，观众席却一片黑。
senses.why: Inside a theatre the word narrows from the whole building to the half built for ears rather than for performers.
senses.whyCN: 在剧场内部，这个词从整栋建筑缩小到「为耳朵而建」的那一半，而不是为演员建的那一半。

senses.title: A performance building
senses.definition: a whole building designed for concerts, lectures or large public events
senses.definitionCN: 为音乐会、演讲或大型公共活动而建的整栋建筑
senses.example: The city built an auditorium beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市在河边建了一座演出厅。
senses.why: American cities named grand public halls with the word, so it grew from a room to a building.
senses.whyCN: 美国城市用这个词命名大型公共厅堂，于是它从「房间」长成了「整栋建筑」。

senses.title: A large lecture room
senses.definition: a big teaching room with rising rows of seats facing one speaker
senses.definitionCN: 座位逐排升高、朝向一位讲授者的大教室
senses.example: First-year lectures are held in the largest auditorium.
senses.exampleCN: 一年级的大课在最大的阶梯教室上。
senses.why: This keeps the original Latin university sense: a room where hearers sit before a reader.
senses.whyCN: 这保留了拉丁语最初的大学义：听者坐在朗读者面前的房间。

senses.title: The people in the hall
senses.definition: the audience itself, named after the space it occupies
senses.definitionCN: 以所在空间代指的听众整体
senses.example: The auditorium rose to its feet at the end.
senses.exampleCN: 结束时全场听众起立。
senses.why: A container word can stand for what it contains, so the hall becomes the people inside it.
senses.whyCN: 容器词可以代指其中所装之物，于是「厅」变成了「厅里的人」。

intro.en: Auditorium is the place noun of the hearing family: audit- plus -orium, a room built so that people can hear.
intro.cn: auditorium 是「听」词族的场所名词：audit- 加 -orium，一间为了让人听清而建的房间。

items.en: Audire meant to hear; its participle stem audit- carried the idea into nouns of place.
items.cn: audire 意为「听」，其分词词干 audit- 把这个意思带进了场所名词。

items.en: Auditor meant a hearer, and in a school it meant a student who sat and listened.
items.cn: auditor 意为「听者」，在学校语境里指坐着听讲的学生。

items.en: In Latin the word named a lecture room or school, the place where hearers sat.
items.cn: 在拉丁语中这个词指讲堂或学校，即听者就座的地方。

items.en: English borrowed it in the eighteenth century for a place designed for listening.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入，指专为「听」而设计的场所。

items.en: American cities built large public halls and called them auditoriums, widening the word from a room to a building.
items.cn: 美国城市兴建大型公共厅堂并这样称呼它们，词义从房间扩大到整栋建筑。

items.en: Today it also names the seating area of a theatre, opposite the stage, and by extension the audience itself.
items.cn: 如今它也指剧场中与舞台相对的观众席，并引申指全场听众。

note.en: The look-alike group is the hearing family; the near-meaning group sorts large spaces by what they are built for.
note.cn: 形近组是「听」词族；近义组按用途区分各种大型空间。

entries.definition: a hearer, or a checker of accounts
entries.definitionCN: 听者；查账的人，同根。

entries.definition: relating to hearing
entries.definitionCN: 听觉的；同根形容词。

entries.definition: an official check of accounts
entries.definitionCN: 审计；同根的基础词。

entries.definition: bold or reckless
entries.definitionCN: 大胆的；只是形近，词源不同。

entries.definition: a large room for meetings or meals
entries.definitionCN: 大厅；泛指大型房间，不强调「听」。

entries.definition: a building for plays, with stage and seating
entries.definitionCN: 剧院；包含舞台与观众席的整体。

entries.definition: a round space with rising seats around it
entries.definitionCN: 圆形剧场；座位环绕，词源与「听」无关。

entries.definition: a hall where a whole school or body meets
entries.definitionCN: 集会厅；强调聚集，而非声学设计。

normalIntro.en: Auditorium is audit- plus -orium: the place where hearing happens.
normalIntro.cn: auditorium 就是 audit- 加 -orium：发生「听」这件事的地方。

normal.en: The ending -orium marks a place, as in sanatorium.
normal.cn: 词尾 -orium 表示场所，如疗养院。

normal.en: In a theatre the auditorium faces the stage.
normal.cn: 在剧场里观众席与舞台相对。

normal.en: American use can mean a whole building.
normal.cn: 美式用法可以指整栋建筑。

normal.en: Both auditoriums and auditoria are plurals.
normal.cn: 两种复数形式都成立，后者更书面。

normal.en: Audience is the people; auditorium is the room.
normal.cn: 听众指人，礼堂指房间。

abstract.en: Picture rows of seats all leaning toward one voice.
abstract.cn: 想象一排排座位都朝一个声音倾去。

abstract.en: Picture a dark sea of faces below a lit stage.
abstract.cn: 想象亮舞台下一片暗色的脸海。

abstract.en: Picture sound reaching the very last row.
abstract.cn: 想象声音一直送到最后一排。

examples.en: The auditorium holds eight hundred people.
examples.cn: 这座礼堂能容纳八百人。

examples.en: We sat near the back of the auditorium.
examples.cn: 我们坐在观众席靠后的位置。

examples.en: Two new auditoria were added to the campus.
examples.cn: 校园里新增了两座礼堂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：audit「听」加 -orium「场所」——专门用来听的房子就是礼堂；剧场里听的那一片座位也是它。

root: 拉丁语 audire「听」的分词词干 audit- 加场所后缀 -orium，构成 auditorium「讲堂、听讲之处」；十八世纪进入英语，美式英语扩为大型演出厅，并指剧场观众席。

sensesIntro.en: A place for hearing grows from a school hall to a whole building, then narrows to the seating half of a theatre, and finally stands for the people in it.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「听的场所」从学校礼堂长成整栋建筑，又缩小为剧场的观众席那一半，最后代指坐在里面的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of seats facing one direction so a voice can reach the last row
core.cn: 核心意象：一排排座位朝着同一方向，让声音送到最后一排

branches.en: a school hall for ceremonies
branches.cn: 举行典礼的学校礼堂

branches.en: the dark half facing the stage
branches.cn: 朝着舞台的暗色那一半

branches.en: a public building for concerts
branches.cn: 供音乐会的公共建筑

branches.en: a big lecture room with rising seats
branches.cn: 座位升高的阶梯大教室

branches.en: the hall standing for its people
branches.cn: 以厅代指满场的人

intro.en: The place ending -orium joins the hearing stem; the same stem gives the person, the act and the adjective.
intro.cn: 场所词尾 -orium 接在「听」的词干上；同一词干还给出指人、指行为与指性质的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin auditorium meant a lecture room, from auditor, a hearer, from audire, to hear.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 auditorium 意为讲堂，来自 auditor「听者」，再来自 audire「听」。

items.example: an auditor in the back row

latinEntries.example: Auditor is the person inside the room.

definition_zh: 濒危的；有灭绝危险的；受到威胁的
definition_en: in danger of dying out completely, especially of a species whose numbers have fallen dangerously low
core_image: 一只动物站在不断缩小的一块浮冰上，四周的水面一步步逼近
scene: 这里指「濒危的」。 The last wild population is endangered by poaching and habitat loss.
sceneCN: 这里 endangered 指「有灭绝危险的」（第 1 个义项：种群数量降到危险低位，随时可能彻底消失）；句意为最后的野生种群正受盗猎与生境丧失的威胁。图中可辨识物件：缩小的浮冰、逼近的水面、远处的枪影、被砍倒的树线。

pos.zh: 濒危的；有灭绝危险的；受到威胁的
endanger 的过去式与过去分词：使……陷入危险

senses.title: A species at risk of dying out
senses.definition: having so few individuals left that the species may soon disappear
senses.definitionCN: 剩余个体太少，该物种可能很快消失
senses.example: The last wild population is endangered by poaching and habitat loss.
senses.exampleCN: 最后的野生种群正受盗猎与生境丧失的威胁。
senses.why: endanger means to put into danger, and the adjective simply says the danger is now upon the species.
senses.whyCN: endanger 意为「使陷入危险」，形容词就是说明危险已经落到该物种头上。

senses.title: A legal listing status
senses.titleCN: 法律上的濒危名录身份
senses.definition: formally listed by a government as a species in danger of extinction, with protection attached
senses.definitionCN: 被政府正式列入有灭绝危险的物种名录，并附带保护措施
senses.example: The fish was declared endangered under the act in 1985.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鱼在 1985 年依据该法被列为濒危。
senses.why: a statute cannot protect a vague condition, so the adjective became a formal status that a government can list, fund and enforce.
senses.whyCN: 法律无法保护一种模糊的状况，因此这个形容词变成政府可以列名、拨款与执行的正式身份。

senses.title: The middle rung of a ranking
senses.titleCN: 受威胁等级中的一档（低于极危）
senses.definition: the category between vulnerable and critically endangered on a conservation ranking
senses.definitionCN: 保护等级排序中介于易危与极危之间的一档
senses.example: The species moved from vulnerable to endangered last year.
senses.exampleCN: 该物种去年从易危升为濒危。
senses.why: once conservationists ranked risk, the word became a rung on the ladder rather than a vague alarm.
senses.whyCN: 当保护工作者给风险排序，这个词就成了阶梯上的一档，而不再是模糊的警报。

senses.title: A habitat or ecosystem under threat
senses.titleCN: 受威胁的生境或生态系统
senses.definition: said of a habitat or ecosystem whose existence is threatened
senses.definitionCN: 指生存受到威胁的生境或生态系统
senses.example: The endangered wetland supports three rare orchids.
senses.exampleCN: 这片受威胁的湿地养着三种稀有兰花。
senses.why: a place can be at risk just as a species can, so the adjective attaches to the ground itself when the ground may disappear.
senses.whyCN: 地点也像物种一样会陷入危险，因此当地面本身可能消失时，这个形容词就落到土地上。

senses.title: A language losing its speakers
senses.titleCN: 使用人数锐减、可能消亡的语言
senses.definition: said of a language whose speakers are falling and may stop using it altogether
senses.definitionCN: 指使用者不断减少、可能彻底停用的语言
senses.example: The endangered dialect survives in two villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这门濒危方言只在两个村子里留存。
senses.why: a language is carried by speakers, so the same adjective fits when the number of carriers falls sharply.
senses.whyCN: 语言由使用者承载，因此当承载者数量骤减时，同一个形容词同样适用。

senses.title: A craft or tradition at risk
senses.titleCN: 濒临失传的手艺或传统
senses.definition: said of a practice that few people still perform and that may vanish
senses.definitionCN: 指已少有人实践、可能消失的做法
senses.example: Copper engraving is an endangered craft in this region.
senses.exampleCN: 铜版雕刻在这一带是濒临失传的手艺。
senses.why: a craft exists only while hands practise it, so it can be endangered in exactly the way a species is.
senses.whyCN: 手艺只在有人动手实践时存在，因此它可以像物种一样濒危。

senses.title: Simply in danger
senses.titleCN: 泛指处于危险之中（旧义）
senses.definition: in danger generally, of a person, reputation or plan, as in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 泛指人或名誉、计划处于危险，属较早用法
senses.example: His reputation, endangered by the rumour, needed a public answer.
senses.exampleCN: 受流言所危的名誉需要一次公开回应。
senses.why: the general sense came first, and the species sense is the specialization that took over in the twentieth century.
senses.whyCN: 一般义先出现，物种义是 20 世纪接管主导的特殊化用法。

senses.title: Threatened by a named agent
senses.titleCN: 由某个具体威胁因子所危及
senses.definition: put at risk by a stated cause, which the passive construction usually names
senses.definitionCN: 由句中明说的原因置于险境，被动结构通常点出该原因
senses.example: The colony is endangered by rising sea temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 该群落正受海温上升的威胁。
senses.why: the verb-like frame endangered by keeps the original verbal force visible inside the adjective.
senses.whyCN: endangered by 这一结构让原本的动词力量在形容词里仍然可见。

intro.en: Endangered is en- plus danger plus -ed. Danger comes through Old French from Vulgar Latin dominiarium 'power of a lord', from dominus 'lord'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: endangered 由 en- 加 danger 再加 -ed 构成。danger 经古法语来自通俗拉丁 dominiarium「领主的权力」，源自 dominus「领主」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Dominus 'lord, master' produced Vulgar Latin dominiarium 'power to command', which Old French shortened to dangier.
items.cn: dominus「领主、主人」产生通俗拉丁 dominiarium「支配之权」，古法语把它压缩为 dangier。

items.en: In Old French dangier meant 'dominion, power over someone', and only later 'risk, peril'; English took the later sense.
items.cn: 古法语 dangier 意为「支配、对某人的权力」，较晚才转为「风险、危险」；英语吸收的是较晚的义项。

items.en: English danger is recorded from the thirteenth century, and by the fourteenth it meant peril rather than power.
items.cn: 英语 danger 在 13 世纪有记录，到 14 世纪已指危险而非权力。

items.en: The verb endanger is recorded in the fifteenth century and the adjective endangered in the seventeenth, both meaning 'put or be in peril'.
items.cn: 动词 endanger 在 15 世纪有记录，形容词 endangered 在 17 世纪，二者都表示「使／处于危险中」。

items.en: The conservation sense dates from the mid twentieth century; the United States passed an Endangered Species Preservation Act in 1966 and a stronger Endangered Species Act in 1973.
items.cn: 保护义始于 20 世纪中期；美国 1966 年通过《濒危物种保存法》，1973 年通过更强的《濒危物种法》。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest citation for endangered applied to a species is not precisely recorded, and the shift of dangier from 'power' to 'peril' has competing explanations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：endangered 用于物种的最早书证没有确切记录；dangier 从「权力」转向「危险」的过程存在多种解释。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same danger family that are easily confused; group two holds the risk labels that conservation uses in a fixed order.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 danger 词族、容易混淆的形式；第二组是保护工作按固定次序使用的风险等级标签。

entries.definition: Describes something that can harm others, such as a dangerous road. Endangered describes something that may be harmed.
entries.definitionCN: 描述会伤害他者的事物，如危险的道路；endangered 描述可能受到伤害的对象。

entries.definition: To put something at risk; endangered is the resulting state, and endangered by names the agent.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物陷入危险；endangered 是结果状态，endangered by 点出施害者。

entries.definition: The state of being at risk, or the act of putting something at risk; it is used in law and in language studies.
entries.definitionCN: 指处于风险的状态或使之陷入风险的行为；用于法律与语言研究。

entries.definition: The peril itself; endangered says that this peril has attached to a particular species or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指危险本身；endangered 说明这种危险已落到某个物种或事物上。

entries.definition: In United States law, a species likely to become endangered soon; it sits below endangered in severity.
entries.definitionCN: 在美国法律中指很可能在近期变为濒危的物种；严重程度低于 endangered。

entries.definition: Likely to be harmed because of weakness or exposure; in conservation it is a milder category than endangered.
entries.definitionCN: 因脆弱或暴露而容易受损；在保护等级中比 endangered 轻。

entries.definition: A formal synonym for put in danger; it appears in conservation writing but carries no legal listing.
entries.definitionCN: 「陷入危险」的正式同义词；见于保护写作，但不带法律名录含义。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for exposure to harm; endangered is its technical, species-specific counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指暴露于伤害的日常说法；endangered 是它在物种语境中的技术化对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: en- 'in' + danger + -ed: danger has been put into the species.
normal.cn: en-「进入」+ danger + -ed：危险已被放进这个物种身上。

normal.en: The family runs endanger, endangered, endangerment, danger, dangerous.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 endanger、endangered、endangerment、danger、dangerous。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: endangered species, critically endangered, endangered language.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：濒危物种、极危、濒危语言。

normal.en: The conservation ladder runs least concern, near threatened, vulnerable, endangered, critically endangered.
normal.cn: 保护等级阶梯依次为无危、近危、易危、濒危、极危。

normal.en: Danger itself came from a word for a lord's power, not from a word for harm.
normal.cn: danger 本身来自表示领主权力的词，而非表示伤害的词。

abstract.en: Picture an animal on ice that melts a little every day.
abstract.cn: 想象一只动物站在每天缩小一点的冰上。

abstract.en: Picture a language with two old speakers and no children listening.
abstract.cn: 想象一门语言只剩两位老人会说，没有孩子在听。

abstract.en: Picture a craft kept alive by one pair of hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一门手艺只靠一双手维持。

examples.en: The orchid is endangered because its pollinator has vanished.
examples.cn: 这种兰花因传粉者消失而濒危。

examples.en: Endangered species receive legal protection on both land and water.
examples.cn: 濒危物种在陆地与水域都受到法律保护。

examples.en: The endangered language is taught in one village school.
examples.cn: 这门濒危语言在一所村校里教授。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en（放进）+ danger（危险）+ ed」——危险已经落在它头上 → 濒危的、受威胁的

root: en-（使进入）+ danger（危险，经古法语 dangier 来自通俗拉丁 dominiarium「领主之权」，源自 dominus「领主」）+ -ed。英语 endangered。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one situation: danger is placed on something, and that situation is then read as a species, a legal listing, a rank, a habitat, a language, a craft, a reputation and a named cause.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个处境展开：危险被放到某物身上，这个处境再被读成物种、法律名录、等级、生境、语言、手艺、名誉与一个被点名的成因。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an animal on a shrinking floe while the water closes in.
core.cn: 核心意象：动物站在缩小的浮冰上，水面步步逼近。

branches.en: DANGER ATTACHED: from a species to an old reputation, the peril is real and present.
branches.cn: 危险附着：从物种到旧式名誉，危险都真实而当下。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL LABELS: law lists it, and rankings place it on a ladder.
branches.cn: 制度标签：法律把它列名，等级把它放上阶梯。

branches.en: PLACE AT RISK: a habitat can be endangered as well as its inhabitants.
branches.cn: 地点受危：生境本身也会濒危，不只有其中的生物。

branches.en: PRACTICE FADING: languages and crafts lose their carriers.
branches.cn: 实践式微：语言与手艺失去承载者。

branches.en: NAMED CAUSE: the passive frame asks who or what is doing the endangering.
branches.cn: 点明成因：被动结构追问是谁或什么在施加危险。

intro.en: Endangered is a native English construction of prefix plus noun plus suffix, built on a French borrowing rather than on a Latin root.
intro.cn: endangered 是英语本族的前缀加名词再加后缀的构造，基底是法语借词，而非拉丁词根。

latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁基底是 dominus「领主」，由此得 dominiarium，再经古法语 dangier 得英语 danger；en- 与 -ed 是英语词缀。

definition_zh: 导电的；导热的；有助于……的
definition_en: able to carry heat or electricity, or able to help something happen
core_image: 一条铜带把热量从火焰这头送到那头，中途几乎没有丢掉什么
scene: 实验室里，学生把一根铜棒的一端放进火焰，另一端的蜡很快开始融化。 The copper strip proved so conductive that the wax melted within seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 conductive 指「导热的」（第 2 个义项：能传递热）；句意为铜条导热太好，蜡几秒就融化了。图中可辨识物件：铜棒、火焰、蜡块、温度计。

pos.zh: 导电的；导热的；可传导的
有助于……的；有利于……发生的

senses.title: Carrying electric charge
senses.definition: able to carry electric charge from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 能把电荷从一处送到另一处
senses.example: The salt solution becomes conductive once the ions separate.
senses.exampleCN: 离子一旦分开，盐溶液就变得导电。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant leading along, and the suffix adds a tendency: a conductive material tends to let charge travel through it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「引导」，后缀又加上「倾向」：导电材料倾向于让电荷穿过。

senses.title: Carrying heat
senses.definition: able to carry heat from a warmer place to a cooler one
senses.definitionCN: 能把热从较热处传到较冷处
senses.example: The copper strip proved so conductive that the wax melted within seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 铜条导热太好，蜡几秒就融化了。
senses.why: Heat and charge both move through the same solids in the same way, so one adjective serves the two cases.
senses.whyCN: 热与电荷在同样的固体里以同样的方式移动，因此一个形容词同时服务两种情形。

senses.title: Able to pass something through
senses.titleCN: 可传导的：能让某种能量通过
senses.definition: able to let a form of energy or a signal pass through a medium
senses.definitionCN: 能让某种能量或信号穿过介质
senses.example: The gel is conductive to ultrasound but not to light.
senses.exampleCN: 这种凝胶能传导超声，却不能让光通过。
senses.why: The core of the word is passage rather than electricity, so it applies to sound, light and other signals when a medium carries them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是「通过」，而不是电，因此当介质运送声音、光等信号时也能用它。

senses.title: Strongly conductive
senses.titleCN: 导电或导热性强的；良导的
senses.definition: having a high ability to carry charge or heat
senses.definitionCN: 传导电荷或热的能力很强
senses.example: Silver is the most conductive metal, which is why it is used in contacts.
senses.exampleCN: 银是导电性最强的金属，因此常用于触点。
senses.why: The adjective is gradable: materials are compared by how much they pass, so it also means strongly conductive.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词有程度差别：材料按通过量比较，因此它也指「传导性强的」。

senses.title: Of conductance
senses.titleCN: 电导的；与传导率有关的
senses.definition: relating to conductivity or to the measured ease of passing current
senses.definitionCN: 与传导率或以数值衡量的通电难易有关
senses.example: The team measured the conductive properties of the alloy at low temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 团队测量了这种合金在低温下的电导特性。
senses.why: Once the ability is expressed as a number, the adjective attaches to measurements and technical descriptions.
senses.whyCN: 当这种能力被表示成数值，形容词就附着在测量与技术描述上。

senses.title: Of sound reaching the ear
senses.titleCN: 传导性听力损失的（医学）
senses.definition: relating to sound being blocked in its path to the inner ear rather than to the nerve
senses.definitionCN: 指声音在到达内耳的路途中受阻，而不是神经本身出问题
senses.example: Conductive hearing loss improves when the blockage is removed.
senses.exampleCN: 传导性听力损失在阻塞被清除后会改善。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the word for a pathway problem: the sound is fine, but its conduction through the ear is interrupted.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了这个词来表示通路问题：声音本身没问题，是它在耳内的传导被中断了。

senses.title: Helping something happen
senses.definition: tending to help or promote a result, often followed by to
senses.definitionCN: 倾向于促成某种结果，常接 to
senses.example: A quiet room is conductive to concentration.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的屋子有助于集中注意力。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the idea of a path: conditions that are conductive to something make it easy for that thing to travel toward its result.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻保留了通路的意思：有利于某事的条件，让那件事更容易走向结果。

senses.title: Likely to set off a reaction
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：容易引发某种结果或氛围的
senses.definition: likely to bring about a particular mood, reaction or outcome
senses.definitionCN: 容易带来某种气氛、反应或结果
senses.example: That rumour was conductive to panic in the crowded hall.
senses.exampleCN: 那条谣言很容易在拥挤的大厅里引发恐慌。
senses.why: The abstract sense pushes the path idea into cause: what is conductive to panic lets panic spread as if along a wire.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把通路推向因果：有利于恐慌的东西，让恐慌像沿导线一样扩散。

intro.en: Conductive is conduct plus the Latin suffix -ive, from the verb conducere 'to lead together'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: conductive 是 conduct 加拉丁后缀 -ive 构成，源自动词 conducere「一起引导」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Conducere joined com- 'together' with ducere 'to lead', giving the sense of bringing something along a path.
items.cn: conducere 由 com-「一起」与 ducere「引导」构成，意为把某物沿一条路带过去。

items.en: Later Latin formed conductivus, 'tending to lead or carry', which English took as conductive in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语构成 conductivus，意为「有引导、运送倾向的」，英语在十七世纪借入作 conductive。

items.en: Early English uses described substances that carry heat or fluid, long before the word was tied to electricity.
items.cn: 早期英语用法描述能传热或传流体的物质，远在它被绑定到电之前。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century experimenters applied it to materials that pass charge, and conductivity became its measured noun.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪的实验者用它指能通过电荷的材料，conductivity 成为其可测量的名词形式。

items.en: The phrase conductive to, meaning helpful to a result, is recorded from the seventeenth century and grew alongside the physical sense.
items.cn: conductive to 表示有助于某种结果，自十七世纪起有记录，与物理义同时发展。

items.en: Twentieth-century audiology used conductive for sound blocked on its way through the outer or middle ear.
items.cn: 二十世纪的听力学用 conductive 指声音在外耳或中耳通道上受阻。

note.en: Group one holds derivatives of the same Latin verb; group two holds words about passing or helping things through.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁动词的派生词；第二组是关于让东西通过或促成的词。

entries.definition: To carry or lead; conductive describes the ability to do so.
entries.definitionCN: 运送或引导；conductive 描述具备这种能力。

entries.definition: The process of carrying heat or charge through a material.
entries.definitionCN: 热或电荷通过材料的过程。

entries.definition: The material or person that carries; the adjective describes it.
entries.definitionCN: 承载或引导的材料或人；形容词描述这一性质。

entries.definition: How well a material conducts, expressed as a number.
entries.definitionCN: 材料传导能力的数值表示。

entries.definition: Actively sending energy or signals onward, often with a device attached.
entries.definitionCN: 主动把能量或信号送出去，常涉及具体装置。

entries.definition: Allows fluids or gases to pass through pores; not used for charge.
entries.definitionCN: 允许流体或气体穿过孔隙；不用于电荷。

entries.definition: Preventing heat or charge from passing; the exact reverse of conductive.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止热或电荷通过，正是 conductive 的反面。

entries.definition: The plain word for conditions that help something succeed, close to conductive to.
entries.definitionCN: 表示条件有助于成功的平实说法，接近 conductive to。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb, the real suffixes, and the real split between electricity and help.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、真实的后缀，以及电学义与「有助于」义的真实分工。

normal.en: The root is lead: conduct, conductor, conduction and conductivity all describe something travelling along a path.
normal.cn: 词根是「引导」：conduct、conductor、conduction、conductivity 都描述沿通路行进的过程。

normal.en: The suffix -ive adds a tendency: a conductive material tends to let energy through.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ive 加「倾向」：导电材料倾向于让能量通过。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physics: conductive material, electrically conductive, thermally conductive.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理义：导电材料、电导的、导热的。

normal.en: The same adjective turns social: a quiet room is conductive to concentration.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词也转向社会语境：安静的屋子有助于集中注意力。

normal.en: Medicine keeps the path picture: conductive hearing loss is a blockage on the way in, not a damaged nerve.
normal.cn: 医学保留了通路图景：传导性听力损失是入口堵塞，而不是神经受损。

abstract.en: Picture heat walking down a copper rod hand over hand.
abstract.cn: 想象热沿着铜棒一手接一手地往下走。

abstract.en: Picture a hall with the doors open, so sound walks in without effort.
abstract.cn: 想象一座门都敞开的大厅，声音毫不费力地走进来。

abstract.en: Picture conditions arranged like rails, so an outcome can roll toward you.
abstract.cn: 想象条件摆成轨道，让结果顺着轨道滚向你。

examples.en: The new polymer is conductive but still flexible enough to print on.
examples.cn: 这种新聚合物能导电，又软到可以印刷。

examples.en: Poorly conductive walls let the heat escape within an hour.
examples.cn: 导热差的墙一小时内就把热量放跑了。

examples.en: A regular routine is conductive to better sleep.
examples.cn: 规律的作息有助于改善睡眠。

dict_mnemonic.text: con-（一起）+ duct（引导）+ -ive（有……倾向的）——倾向于让能量通过 → 导电的、导热的；有助于的

root: 拉丁 conducere（一起引导）→ 晚期拉丁 conductivus（有运送倾向的）→ 英语 conductive；电学义与「有助于」义都从「沿路引过去」发展而来。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with charge and heat passing through a material, widen to any energy, become a measured property, turn medical, and end with conditions that help a result along.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从电荷与热穿过材料开始，扩展到任何能量，变成可测量的性质，转入医学，最后落到有助于结果的条件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a copper strip passing heat from a flame to a lump of wax.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条铜带把热从火焰送到一块蜡。

branches.en: The electric case and its strong form: charge passes, and some metals pass it very well.
branches.cn: 电学情形及其强形式：电荷通过，有些金属通过得极好。

branches.en: The thermal case, where what travels is heat.
branches.cn: 热学情形，通过的是热。

branches.en: Any energy through any medium, and the number that states how easily it passes.
branches.cn: 任何能量穿过任何介质，以及说明通过难易的数值。

branches.en: Sound blocked on its path through the ear, so the pathway itself is the problem.
branches.cn: 声音在耳内通道上受阻，问题出在通路本身。

branches.en: Conditions that help a result travel toward you, or let a mood spread.
branches.cn: 有助于结果走向你的条件，或让某种情绪扩散的条件。

intro.en: Conductive is the adjective of conduct, and the whole family attaches ordinary suffixes to the Latin stem duct-.
intro.cn: conductive 是 conduct 的形容词，整个词族都在拉丁词干 duct- 上加普通后缀。

latinIntro.en: Conducere and its participle conductus supply the stem; conductivus is a later Latin adjective, and English built conductor, conduction, conductivity and conductance on the same base.
latinIntro.cn: conducere 及其分词 conductus 提供词干；conductivus 是晚期拉丁形容词，英语又在同一词基上构造 conductor、conduction、conductivity 与 conductance。

items.meaningCN: 传导；引导；管理（前缀加引导词根，动作本身）

items.meaning: tending to carry heat or charge
items.meaningCN: 有传导倾向的（加倾向后缀，动作转性质）
items.example: The sheet is conductive on one side.

items.meaning: the passing of heat or charge through matter
items.meaningCN: 传导过程（加过程后缀，动作转过程）
items.exampleCN: 传导解释了手柄为什么发热。

items.meaningCN: 传导率（再加性质后缀，性质转数值）
items.example: Its conductivity is close to copper.

items.meaning: a material or person that carries
items.meaningCN: 导体；指挥（加执行者后缀，动作转执行者）

items.meaning: the ease with which a path passes current
items.meaningCN: 电导（加状态后缀，动作转通路能力）
items.example: Conductance doubles when the wire thickens.

items.meaning: a material that conducts only under set conditions
items.meaningCN: 半导体（加「一半」前缀，导体性质被限定）
items.example: A semiconductor can switch the current.

items.meaningCN: 不导电的（加否定前缀，性质被取消）

items.meaning: becoming conductive when light falls on it
items.meaningCN: 光导的（加「光」前缀，传导条件变成光照）
items.example: The sensor uses a photoconductive layer.
items.exampleCN: 传感器使用一层光导材料。

senses.title: A long narrow cut to expose soil layers
senses.titleCN: 为暴露土层而挖的窄长沟
senses.definition: a long narrow hole dug down through soil so that its layers can be seen
senses.definitionCN: 向下挖穿土壤的长窄坑，以便观察各层
senses.example: The excavation trench exposed three layers of occupation debris.
senses.exampleCN: 这条探沟露出了三层人类活动堆积。
senses.why: excavation names the digging out and trench names the long cut, so the phrase describes both the act and the shape.
senses.whyCN: excavation 指挖出，trench 指长形切口，因此短语同时描述动作与形状。

senses.title: An archaeological digging unit
senses.definition: a controlled unit of archaeological digging used to record stratigraphy
senses.definitionCN: 用于记录地层关系的受控考古挖掘单位
senses.example: Each excavation trench is photographed before any soil is removed.
senses.exampleCN: 每条探沟在取土前都要拍照。
senses.why: a controlled unit is what separates research digging from mere hole-making.
senses.whyCN: 受控单位正是把研究性发掘与单纯挖坑区分开的东西。

senses.title: A test pit or trial trench
senses.definition: a small trench dug first to test whether a site is worth full excavation
senses.definitionCN: 为判断遗址是否值得全面发掘而先挖的小沟
senses.example: A trial excavation trench showed that the wall continued westward.
senses.exampleCN: 一条试掘探沟显示这堵墙继续向西延伸。
senses.why: a trial cut is the smallest version of the method, used before committing to full excavation.
senses.whyCN: 试掘沟是这套方法的最小版本，用于在全面发掘前试探。

senses.title: A section for stratigraphic recording
senses.definition: the exposed vertical face of a trench, drawn and photographed as a stratigraphic section
senses.definitionCN: 探沟露出的垂直面，作为地层剖面绘制并拍照
senses.example: The east face of the excavation trench shows a buried plough soil.
senses.exampleCN: 探沟东壁显示出一层被埋的耕作土。
senses.why: the exposed face is what gets drawn and photographed, turning the cut into a record.
senses.whyCN: 露出的壁面会被绘制与拍照，把切口变成记录。

senses.title: A drainage or foundation trench
senses.definition: a long cut dug for pipes, foundations or drainage rather than for research
senses.definitionCN: 为管道、地基或排水而非研究挖出的长沟
senses.example: Workers dug an excavation trench for the new water main.
senses.exampleCN: 工人为新供水主管挖了一条沟槽。
senses.why: the same shape serves engineering, so the phrase is not limited to archaeology.
senses.whyCN: 同一形状也服务于工程，因此短语并不限于考古。

senses.title: A defensive trench
senses.definition: a long cut used as a barrier or protected position, as in military earthworks
senses.definitionCN: 作为屏障或防护阵地的长沟，如军事土工作业
senses.example: The old excavation trench was later reused as a drainage channel.
senses.exampleCN: 那条旧战壕后来被改作排水沟。
senses.why: a defensive ditch is another practical use of a long cut.
senses.whyCN: 防御沟是长形切口的另一种实用。

senses.title: The open cut itself
senses.definition: the open void left by digging, including its sides and floor
senses.definitionCN: 挖掘后留下的敞开的沟体，包括两侧与底面
senses.example: Rainwater collected at the bottom of the excavation trench.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水积在探沟底部。
senses.why: the open void is the physical result of digging, distinct from its research purpose.
senses.whyCN: 敞开的沟体是挖掘的物理结果，区别于其研究目的。

senses.title: A method of systematic excavation
senses.definition: the technique of using narrow trenches to sample a large area efficiently
senses.definitionCN: 用窄沟高效取样大面积的发掘技术
senses.example: The team used an excavation trench grid to map the whole field.
senses.exampleCN: 团队用探沟网格测绘整片田野。
senses.why: a grid of narrow cuts samples a large area, which is the method sense.
senses.whyCN: 用窄沟组成的网格对大区域取样，这就是「方法」义。

intro.en: Excavation trench joins a Latin verb meaning 'hollow out' to an Old French noun meaning 'a cut'. Excavare is ex- 'out' plus cavus 'hollow'; trenchier meant 'to cut', and its own deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: excavation trench 把意为「挖空」的拉丁动词与意为「切出的沟」的古法语名词接在一起。excavare 是 ex-「向外」加 cavus「空腔」；trenchier 意为「切」，其更深来源不确定。

items.en: Cavus meant 'hollow, a cavity', the image behind excavation.
items.cn: cavus 意为「空的、空腔」，是 excavation 背后的意象。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus cavare 'to make hollow' produced excavare, 'to hollow out, dig out'.
items.cn: ex-「向外」加 cavare「使空」构成 excavare，意为「挖空、挖出」。

items.en: Trenchier meant 'to cut', and its noun trenche named a cut or a ditch; the deeper origin of the verb is uncertain.
items.cn: trenchier 意为「切」，其名词 trenche 指切口或沟；这个动词的更早来源不确定。

items.en: English trench first named a ditch or a cut in the ground, later a military defensive ditch.
items.cn: 英语 trench 最初指地上的沟或切口，后来指军事防御沟。

items.en: Excavation became the standard term for controlled digging, and the phrase excavation trench named its basic unit.
items.cn: excavation 成为受控挖掘的标准术语，短语 excavation trench 命名其基本单位。

items.en: Source uncertain (trench only): the pre-French origin of trenchier is not settled, and suggestions linking it to Latin truncare remain hypotheses.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅 trench）：trenchier 在法语之前的来源未定，把它与拉丁 truncare 联系起来的说法仍属假说。

note.en: Group one holds digging units easily confused with an excavation trench; group two holds words for holes and cuts in the ground.
note.cn: 第一组是容易与探沟混淆的发掘单位；第二组是表示地面孔洞与切口的词。

entries.definition: A small pit dug to sample a site; a trench is long and narrow, a pit is compact.
entries.definitionCN: 为取样遗址挖的小坑；trench 长而窄，pit 紧凑。

entries.definition: A small exploratory excavation in French archaeology; it is a kind of test trench.
entries.definitionCN: 法国考古学中的小型试掘；是试掘探沟的一种。

entries.definition: A square unit of controlled digging; a trench is long rather than square.
entries.definitionCN: 受控发掘的方形单位；trench 是长形而非方形。

entries.definition: A deep vertical cut or well-like hole; a trench is horizontal in extent.
entries.definitionCN: 深的垂直切口或井状孔；trench 在延伸上是水平的。

entries.tag: a long cut in the ground
entries.definition: A long narrow channel, often for drainage or defence; an excavation trench is defined by its research purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 长窄沟渠，常用于排水或防御；探沟以研究目的界定。

entries.definition: A open cut made for a road or railway; it is engineering, not archaeology.
entries.definitionCN: 为道路或铁路挖开的切口；属工程，不是考古。

entries.tag: a hole dug in the ground
entries.definition: A hole dug for burial, storage or testing; it is not long and narrow.
entries.definitionCN: 为埋葬、储藏或测试挖的坑；不呈长窄形。

entries.definition: A long passage cut or built for water; it stresses flow rather than exposure.
entries.definitionCN: 为水挖成或建成的长通道；强调水流，而非暴露地层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin hollow and the French cut, plus the real field method.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁「空腔」与法语「切」，以及真实的田野方法。

normal.en: excavare is ex- 'out' plus cavus 'hollow': to hollow out.
normal.cn: excavare 是 ex-「向外」加 cavus「空腔」：挖空。

normal.en: trench comes from French trenchier, to cut.
normal.cn: trench 来自法语 trenchier「切」。

normal.en: A trench is long and narrow; a pit is compact.
normal.cn: 探沟长而窄；坑则紧凑。

normal.en: The vertical face of a trench is drawn as a section.
normal.cn: 探沟的垂直面被绘成剖面。

normal.en: Trial trenches test a site before full excavation.
normal.cn: 试掘探沟在全面发掘前测试遗址。

abstract.en: An excavation trench is a thin cut that lets the ground speak in layers.
abstract.cn: 探沟是一道细切口，让大地按层说话。

abstract.en: It is a window made by removing the wall.
abstract.cn: 它是一扇靠拆掉墙才做成的窗。

abstract.en: The trench is temporary, but the section it records lasts in the archive.
abstract.cn: 探沟是临时的，但它记录的剖面在档案里长存。

examples.en: The excavation trench was backfilled at the end of the season.
examples.cn: 探沟在季度结束时被回填。

examples.en: A narrow excavation trench ran across the whole courtyard.
examples.cn: 一条窄探沟横穿整个庭院。

examples.en: The excavation trench revealed a floor of beaten earth.
examples.cn: 这条探沟露出了一层夯土地面。

root: excavation 来自拉丁 excavare「挖空」= ex-「向外」+ cavus「空腔」；trench 来自古法语 trenche「切出的沟」，动词 trenchier 更深来源不确定。短语指考古发掘的窄长探沟。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one cut: exposed layers, an archaeological unit, a trial hole, a recorded section, a service ditch, a defensive ditch, the open void and a sampling method.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一道切口展开：露出的土层、考古单位、试掘孔、记录剖面、管线沟、防御沟、敞开的沟体与取样方法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow vertical slice through the ground, its wall showing stripes of old floors and ash.
core.cn: 核心意象：在地面上切出的一道窄而深的切口，壁面露出旧地面与灰烬的条纹。

branches.en: CUT AND VOID: the act of exposing layers and the open hole it leaves are the same cut in process and result.
branches.cn: 切与空：暴露土层的动作与留下的敞开沟体，是同一道切口的动作面与结果面。

branches.en: RESEARCH UNITS: a controlled digging unit and a small trial cut are the same method at full and at test scale.
branches.cn: 研究单位：受控发掘单位与小试掘沟，是同一方法在全面与试验尺度上。

branches.en: RECORDED FACE: the section turns a hole into a document.
branches.cn: 被记录的壁面：剖面把坑洞变成文件。

branches.en: OTHER CUTS: service and defensive ditches borrow the shape for practical ends.
branches.cn: 其他沟：管线沟与防御沟为实用目的借用同一形状。

branches.en: METHOD: a grid of trenches samples a whole landscape.
branches.cn: 方法：探沟网格对整个地貌取样。

intro.cn: excavation trench 是两词技术短语，一个源自拉丁，一个源自法语，每一半都有自己的词族。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cavus 与 excavare 提供 excavation；古法语 trenche 提供 trench，因此短语有两条独立来源。

definition_zh: n. 圆周；周长；（绕圆一周的）周边
definition_en: the line that goes round a circle, or the distance around it

scene: 她沿着跑道走完一整圈，算出操场周长为四百米。 She walked the track once to measure its circumference.

周边长度

senses.title: The boundary line of a circle
senses.definition: the continuous line that forms the edge of a circle
senses.definitionCN: 构成圆形边缘的连续曲线
senses.example: The fence follows the circumference of the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 篱笆沿着池塘的圆周延伸。
senses.why: Latin circum means around and ferre means to carry.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 circum 意为环绕，ferre 意为携带。

senses.title: The distance around a circle
senses.definition: the measured length of the line around a circle
senses.definitionCN: 绕圆一周所量得的长度
senses.example: Her waist circumference fell by two inches.
senses.exampleCN: 她的腰围减了两英寸。
senses.why: A drawn line became a number you can measure.
senses.whyCN: 画出的线变成可以测量的数值。

intro.en: Circumference joins a Latin prefix of circling to a Latin verb of carrying.
intro.cn: circumference 由表示环绕的拉丁前缀和表示携带的拉丁动词组成。

items.en: Circum means around or on all sides.
items.cn: circum 意为环绕、四周。

items.en: Ferre means to carry or bear.
items.cn: ferre 意为携带、承担。

items.en: The noun means a carrying around, a line drawn around.
items.cn: 该名词意为绕行一周、画出的环线。

items.en: English borrows the term for the edge of a circle.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入几何学指圆的边缘。

items.en: The word also names the distance measured around a body or shape.
items.cn: 现代也指绕物体量出的长度。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the circum- shape; the near-meaning group names other ways round a shape.

entries.definitionCN: 绕行一周的路线。

entries.definition: The facts around an event.

entries.definition: The distance round a shape.

examples.en: They planted flowers around the circumference of the lawn.

examples.en: Doctors recorded the waist circumference of each child.
examples.cn: 医生记录了每个孩子的腰围。

definition_zh: 使受精；给……施肥；使肥沃
definition_en: to join a male and a female cell, or to add nutrients to soil, water or a growing medium
core_image: 一只手把肥料撒进田垄，另一只手在显微镜下把精子送到卵子旁边
scene: 果园里，工人用软毛刷把花粉从一株花移到另一株花的柱头上。 Growers fertilize the rows by hand when the bees are too few to do the work.
sceneCN: 这里 fertilize 指「使（花）受精、给花授粉」（第 5 个义项：人为把配子送到位）；句意为当蜜蜂太少、干不了这活时，种植者就人工给这几行花授粉。

pos.zh: 使受精；使受孕；给……施肥；使肥沃
（土地）变得肥沃

senses.title: Add nutrients to soil
senses.definition: to add substances to soil so that crops grow better
senses.definitionCN: 向土壤添加物质，使作物长得更好
senses.example: They fertilize the vegetable beds every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 他们每年秋天给菜畦施肥。
senses.why: the -ize suffix means 'make', and the root means 'fruitful', so fertilize reads as 'make fruitful'.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ize 意为「使」，词根意为「能结果的」，因此 fertilize 读作「使之结果」。

senses.title: Enrich a body of water
senses.definition: to add nutrients to a lake, pond or sea
senses.definitionCN: 向湖泊、池塘或海洋添加养分
senses.example: Farm runoff fertilizes the bay every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 农场的径流每年春天给海湾带来养分。
senses.why: water is treated exactly like soil: something is added so that growth increases, whether wanted or not.
senses.whyCN: 水被完全当作土壤处理：加入某种东西使生长增加，无论这是否是想要的结果。

senses.title: Join a sperm with an egg
senses.definition: to cause a female reproductive cell to fuse with a male one
senses.definitionCN: 使雌性生殖细胞与雄性生殖细胞融合
senses.example: A single sperm fertilizes the egg within hours of ovulation.
senses.exampleCN: 排卵后数小时内，一枚精子使卵子受精。
senses.why: the verb takes the egg as its object and the sperm as its instrument, so the egg is what becomes fruitful.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词以卵为宾语、以精子为工具，因此变得「能结果」的是卵。

senses.title: Make a female animal pregnant
senses.definition: to cause a female animal to conceive, as in breeding
senses.definitionCN: 使雌性动物怀孕，如育种中所为
senses.example: The stallion fertilized eleven mares that season.
senses.exampleCN: 那匹公马在那个季节使十一匹母马受孕。
senses.why: in animal husbandry the outcome matters more than the cell event, so the verb stands for the whole successful mating.
senses.whyCN: 在畜牧中结果比细胞事件更重要，动词因此代表整个成功的交配过程。

senses.title: Move pollen to a flower
senses.definition: to bring pollen to the stigma of a flower, by hand or by a chosen insect
senses.definitionCN: 把花粉送到花的柱头上，靠人工或选定的昆虫
senses.example: Workers fertilize the vanilla flowers with a small wooden needle.
senses.exampleCN: 工人用小木针给香草花授粉。
senses.why: in flowering plants the pollen must arrive before fusion can happen, so the verb covers the delivery stage too.
senses.whyCN: 在开花植物中，花粉必须先到达才可能融合，因此这个动词也覆盖了投递阶段。

senses.title: Make land productive
senses.definition: to improve land so that it can support more growth
senses.definitionCN: 改良土地，使其能支撑更多生长
senses.example: Decades of flooding fertilized the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 数十年的洪水使这片三角洲变得肥沃。
senses.why: this sense drops the nutrient material and keeps only the result: land that bears more than before.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项去掉了养分材料，只保留结果：土地比从前结出更多东西。

senses.title: Enrich the mind or imagination
senses.titleCN: 比喻：丰富、激发思想与想像
senses.definition: to supply something that makes a mind or a plan more productive
senses.definitionCN: 提供某种东西，使头脑或计划更有产出
senses.example: Travel fertilized her imagination more than any classroom did.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行比任何课堂都更能激发她的想像力。
senses.why: the metaphor transfers the soil gesture to thought: an outside substance is added and growth follows.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把给土壤的动作移到思想上：加入外在之物，随后便有生长。

senses.title: Feed a laboratory medium
senses.definition: to add nutrients to a medium in which cells or plants are grown
senses.definitionCN: 向培养细胞或植物的介质中添加养分
senses.example: The team fertilized the culture medium with trace minerals.
senses.exampleCN: 团队向培养基中添加微量元素。
senses.why: a medium is a manufactured soil, so the agricultural verb fits it without any change of sense.
senses.whyCN: 培养基是人造的土壤，因此农业动词原样适用，词义不需改变。

intro.en: Fertilize comes from Medieval Latin fertilizare, built on fertilis 'fruitful', itself ferre 'to bear' plus -ilis 'able'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fertilize 来自中世纪拉丁 fertilizare，建立在 fertilis「能结果的」之上，后者由 ferre「承载」加 -ilis「能够」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ferre 'to bear, carry' is the source of fertile as well as of transfer and refer.
items.cn: ferre「承载、生育」既是 fertile 的来源，也是 transfer 与 refer 的来源。

items.en: Fertilis 'fruitful' is generally explained as ferre plus -ilis, 'able to bear'; the intermediate adjective is not attested in surviving texts.
items.cn: fertilis「能结果的」一般解释为 ferre 加 -ilis「能够承载」；这个中间形容词在现存文献中没有书证。

items.en: Fertilizare meant 'to make fruitful' and was applied to land long before it was applied to gametes.
items.cn: fertilizare 意为「使之结果」，用于土地远早于用于配子。

items.en: English fertilize appears in the seventeenth century in agricultural writing, then spreads to biology in the eighteenth and nineteenth.
items.cn: 英语 fertilize 于 17 世纪出现在农业写作中，18、19 世纪扩展到生物学。

items.en: Source uncertain (first biological date): the first use of the verb for the union of gametes is not precisely dated; the agricultural record is clearer than the biological one.
items.cn: 来源不确定（生物学义的首见年代）：这个动词首次用于配子结合的时间没有确切记载；农业用法的记录比生物学用法更清楚。

note.en: Group one separates the -fer- verbs that differ only by prefix; group two separates verbs of supplying from verbs of joining.
note.cn: 第一组区分只靠前缀不同的 -fer- 动词；第二组区分「供给」类动词与「结合」类动词。

entries.definition: From Latin fermentum 'leaven', not from ferre; it means to break down sugars, so the shared fer- is a coincidence of spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 fermentum「酵素」，并非出自 ferre；意为分解糖分，因此相同的 fer- 只是拼写巧合。

entries.definition: From Latin fomentum 'a warm application'; it means to stir up trouble or apply warmth, with no link to fertility.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 fomentum「热敷物」；意为煽动或热敷，与肥沃无关。

entries.definition: Con- 'together' plus ferre: to bring together in speech, hence to consult or bestow.
entries.definitionCN: con-「一起」加 ferre：在言语中带到一处，因此指商议或授予。

entries.definition: De- 'away' plus ferre: to carry something away to a later time, hence to postpone.
entries.definitionCN: de-「离开」加 ferre：把某事搬到以后的时间，因此指推迟。

entries.definition: To supply what a living thing needs to grow; it names the feeding, while fertilize names making the medium fruitful.
entries.definitionCN: 提供生物生长所需之物；它指喂养，而 fertilize 指使介质变得肥沃。

entries.definition: To transfer pollen to a stigma; this is the delivery step, while fertilize covers the fusion that follows.
entries.definitionCN: 把花粉送到柱头；这是投递步骤，而 fertilize 覆盖其后的融合。

entries.definition: To introduce semen into the reproductive tract by technical means; fertilization may follow or may not.
entries.definitionCN: 用技术手段把精液送入生殖道；之后可能受精，也可能不受精。

entries.definition: A general verb for adding value or nutrients; it lacks the specific 'bearing fruit' image of fertilize.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指增加价值或养分；缺少 fertilize 那种「结果实」的具体意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real farm and lab phrases, and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的农事与实验搭配以及真实同族词。

normal.en: fer- 'bear' + -tilis 'able' + -ize 'make': to make able to bear.
normal.cn: fer-「承载」+ -tilis「能够」+ -ize「使」：使能够承载、结果。

normal.en: Soil, water, eggs, flowers and culture media can all take the same verb.
normal.cn: 土壤、水、卵、花与培养基都能接受同一个动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: fertilize the soil, fertilize an egg, fertilize with manure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：给土壤施肥、使卵受精、用厩肥施肥。

normal.en: The noun pair is regular: fertilize gives fertilization, as -ize gives -ization.
normal.cn: 名词配对很规则：fertilize 派生 fertilization，正如 -ize 派生 -ization。

normal.en: The family runs fertile, fertility, fertilizer, fertilization, self-fertilize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fertile、fertility、fertilizer、fertilization、self-fertilize。

abstract.en: Picture a hand tipping a jar of richness into a field of thin soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一罐养分倒进贫瘠的田里。

abstract.en: Picture a gardener carrying pollen on a brush as if delivering a letter.
abstract.cn: 想象园丁用刷子带着花粉，像在投递一封信。

abstract.en: Picture a mind that reads widely and then produces ideas it could not produce before.
abstract.cn: 想象一个广泛阅读的头脑，随后产出它原本产不出的想法。

examples.en: Farmers fertilize the fields before the spring rains.
examples.cn: 农民在春雨之前给田地施肥。

examples.en: The bees fertilize the apple trees as they gather nectar.
examples.cn: 蜜蜂采蜜时给苹果树授粉。

examples.en: Too much runoff fertilized the pond and choked it with weeds.
examples.cn: 过多的径流给池塘带来了养分，杂草因此疯长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fer（带来）+ til（能够）+ ize（使）」——使卵子或土地能够结果 → 使受精、施肥

root: 拉丁 fertilis「能结果的」= ferre「承载、生育」+ -ilis「能够」；中世纪拉丁 fertilizare「使结果」；英语 fertilize。ferre 的印欧来源一般认为是 *bher-，属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of fertilize all perform one act: something is supplied or brought together so that growth becomes possible.
sensesIntro.cn: fertilize 的八个义项都在做同一件事：供给或促成结合，使生长成为可能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a handful of richness dropped into a medium that could not otherwise bear much.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把养分落进原本长不出多少东西的介质。

branches.en: FEEDING A MEDIUM: soil, water and culture medium are all enriched the same way.
branches.cn: 喂养介质：土壤、水与培养基都以同样方式被加料。

branches.en: JOINING LIVES: one cell meets another, with conception as the animal result.
branches.cn: 生命的结合：一个细胞遇见另一个，在动物身上便成为受孕。

branches.en: DELIVERY FIRST: pollen has to arrive before any fusion can occur.
branches.cn: 先投递：花粉必须先到，融合才可能发生。

branches.en: RESULT WITHOUT MATERIAL: land can simply become more productive.
branches.cn: 无料之果：土地可以只是变得更能出产。

branches.en: MIND AS SOIL: thought is enriched by what is brought in from outside.
branches.cn: 以心为土：思想因外来之物而变得肥沃。

intro.en: Fertilize is a Latin root plus two suffixes, and its family covers farming, biology and medicine.
intro.cn: fertilize 是拉丁词根加两个后缀，其词族覆盖农业、生物学与医学。

latinIntro.en: Latin ferre 'to bear' yields fertilis and fertilizare; English adds fertilize, fertilizer, fertilization and the wider -fer- family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ferre「承载」衍生 fertilis 与 fertilizare；英语再加上 fertilize、fertilizer、fertilization 以及更广的 -fer- 词族。

items.example: The root supplies the sense of bearing fruit.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「结果实」的意思。

items.meaning: to make, to cause to be

items.example: Fertilizer is the thing that fertilizes.
items.exampleCN: fertilizer 就是用来施肥的东西。

items.example: The fertilizer was spread before planting.

items.meaning: able to bear young or crops
items.example: The valley floor is fertile and well watered.
items.exampleCN: 谷底土地肥沃、水源充足。

items.example: Fertility fell after the soil was exhausted.

items.meaning: the act or result of fertilizing
items.example: Fertilization was confirmed under the microscope.
items.exampleCN: 在显微镜下确认了受精。

items.meaning: to fertilize itself with its own gametes
items.example: Some plants self-fertilize when pollinators are absent.
items.exampleCN: 没有传粉者时，有些植物会自花受精。

latinEntries.structure: fertilizatio, fertilizationis (f., Medieval Latin, third declension)

definition_zh: n. 防波堤；起缓冲作用的东西
definition_en: a wall built out into the sea to break the force of waves; also anything that absorbs a force before it arrives
core_image: 一道石堤横在海面，堤外白浪翻卷，堤内水面如镜
scene: 堤外浪高两米，港里却几乎平静。 Beyond the breakwater the waves stood two metres high, while the harbour stayed almost flat.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：breakwater 指防波堤；句意是堤外浪高两米，港内却几乎平静。

pos.zh: 防波堤；缓冲物

senses.title: A wall built into the sea
senses.definition: a wall or barrier built out from the shore to stop waves reaching a harbour
senses.definitionCN: 从岸边伸入水中、阻止波浪抵达港口的墙或屏障
senses.example: The fishing boats waited behind the breakwater.
senses.exampleCN: 渔船在防波堤后等待。
senses.why: Break and water name exactly what it does to the sea.
senses.whyCN: break 与 water 正说明它对海水做了什么。

senses.title: Anything that absorbs a force
senses.definition: something that weakens a shock or pressure before it reaches others
senses.definitionCN: 在冲击或压力抵达他人之前将其削弱的事物
senses.example: Savings acted as a breakwater against the job loss.
senses.exampleCN: 积蓄在失业面前起了一道缓冲。
senses.why: A wall against waves becomes an image for any first line of defence.
senses.whyCN: 挡浪的墙引申为任何第一道防线。

intro.en: Breakwater is a plain English compound of break and water.
intro.cn: breakwater 是 break 与 water 组成的朴素英语复合词。

items.en: Break means to split or to check a force.
items.cn: break 意为使分裂或阻挡力量。

items.en: Waeter means water.
items.cn: waeter 意为水。

items.en: The compound names a wall that checks the sea.
items.cn: 复合词指阻挡海水的墙。

items.en: Steam shipping drives larger breakwaters.
items.cn: 蒸汽航运促使修建更大的防波堤。

items.en: Concrete blocks replace loose stone.
items.cn: 混凝土块取代了散石。

items.en: The image extends to financial buffers.
items.cn: 这一意象延伸到金融缓冲。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the break- compound pattern; the near-meaning group ranks coastal barriers by shape.
note.cn: 形近组共享 break- 复合结构；近义组按形状给海岸屏障排序。

entries.definition: A sudden important advance.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的重要突破。

entries.definition: A failure of a machine or system.
entries.definitionCN: 机器或系统的故障。

entries.definition: Dangerously fast.
entries.definitionCN: 快到危险的。

entries.definition: The act or cost of breaking.
entries.definitionCN: 破损；破损费。

entries.definition: A wall built to stop the sea eroding land.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止海水侵蚀陆地的墙。

entries.definition: A structure projecting into the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 伸入海中的结构。

entries.definition: A platform built out from the shore.
entries.definitionCN: 从岸边伸出的平台。

entries.definition: A low wall that traps sand and slows currents.
entries.definitionCN: 拦沙缓流的矮墙。

normalIntro.en: A breakwater is a wall whose only job is to break water.
normalIntro.cn: breakwater 就是一道唯一职责是「把水打散」的墙。

normal.en: Break means to check a force.
normal.cn: break 意为挡住一股力量。

normal.en: Water is what it fights.
normal.cn: water 是它对抗的东西。

normal.en: So a breakwater stands between sea and harbour.
normal.cn: 所以防波堤站在海与港之间。

normal.en: The harbour behind it stays calm.
normal.cn: 它身后的港口因此平静。

normal.en: Any first buffer can be called a breakwater.
normal.cn: 任何第一道缓冲都可以叫 breakwater。

abstract.en: A hand held up against a wave.
abstract.cn: 举手挡住一道浪。

abstract.en: Still water behind a line of stone.
abstract.cn: 石线之后的静水。

abstract.en: A force arriving and losing itself.
abstract.cn: 一股力量抵达后自行消散。

examples.en: The breakwater was rebuilt after the winter storms.
examples.cn: 防波堤在冬季风暴后重建。

examples.en: Small boats tied up in the shelter of the breakwater.
examples.cn: 小船系在防波堤的庇护处。

examples.en: Emergency savings are a breakwater against sudden debt.
examples.cn: 应急储蓄是抵御突发债务的缓冲。

dict_mnemonic.text: break（打破）+ water（水）——把浪打散的墙，就是防波堤。

root: break（打破）+ water（水）

sensesIntro.en: A breakwater does not stop the sea; it takes the first blow so that the harbour never has to.
sensesIntro.cn: 防波堤并不止住大海，它只是承受第一击，好让港口不必承受。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: white waves outside a stone line, flat water inside
core.cn: 核心意象：石线之外白浪翻卷，石线之内水面平整

branches.en: Fishing boats waiting behind stone.
branches.cn: 石堤后等待的渔船。

branches.en: Concrete blocks piled against the swell.
branches.cn: 堆起来抵御涌浪的混凝土块。

branches.en: Savings set against a job loss.
branches.cn: 为失业准备的积蓄。

branches.en: A first line that takes the shock.
branches.cn: 承受冲击的第一道防线。

branches.en: A barrier that spends itself so others do not.
branches.cn: 消耗自己以免他人受冲击的屏障。

intro.en: Breakwater is a two-word compound; the list below covers its parts and the vocabulary of coastal defence.
intro.cn: breakwater 是两词复合；下面列出它的组成部分以及「海岸防护」词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin moles is a mass or a pier, portus is a harbour, and frangere is to break.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 moles 意为大块或防波堤，portus 意为港口，frangere 意为打破。

latinEntries.exampleCN: moles 产生 mole 与 pier。

definition_zh: 身体语言；体态语；姿势传达的信息
definition_en: the way a person's posture, movements and physical signals communicate meaning without words
core_image: 一个人站着的样子，本身就是一句不用嘴说出的句子
scene: 面试时她不停交叉双臂，面试官把这个信号记在纸上，后来解释道： Her body language suggested resistance.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「通过姿势与动作传达态度的非言语方式」（第 1 个义项：不用词语的身体信号系统）；句意为她的身体语言显得抗拒。

pos.zh: 身体语言；体态语；姿势传达的信息

senses.title: Nonverbal communication through posture and movement
senses.titleCN: 通过姿势与动作进行的非言语交流
senses.definition: the system of signals sent by posture, movement, spacing and touch rather than words
senses.definitionCN: 由姿势、动作、距离与触碰而不是词语发出的信号系统
senses.example: Body language often reveals more than words do.
senses.exampleCN: 身体语言常常比词语透露得更多。
senses.why: The compound treats the body as a language: it has signals, patterns and a reading process, though no grammar of words.
senses.whyCN: 这个合成词把身体当成一种语言：它有信号、模式与解读过程，只是没有词语语法。

senses.title: A person's current posture as an attitude signal
senses.titleCN: 某人当下的姿势所显示的态度
senses.definition: the immediate stance and movements of one person that suggest comfort, confidence or resistance
senses.definitionCN: 一个人当下的站姿与动作，暗示舒适、自信或抗拒
senses.example: His body language was open and relaxed during the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 会议期间他的身体语言开放而放松。
senses.why: At this scale the phrase names one body's present state rather than a general system.
senses.whyCN: 在这个层面上，这个短语命名的是一个身体当下的状态，而不是一般系统。

senses.title: Culturally variable signals
senses.definition: bodily signals whose meaning changes from one culture or community to another
senses.definitionCN: 意义在不同文化或群体之间发生变化的身体信号
senses.example: The same body language can mean different things abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 同样的身体语言在国外可能有不同含义。
senses.why: The body is universal, but the code attached to it is learned, so the phrase can mark cultural difference.
senses.whyCN: 身体是普遍的，但附着其上的代码是习得的，因此这个短语可以标记文化差异。

senses.title: Unconscious cues in psychology
senses.titleCN: 心理学中无意识的线索
senses.definition: bodily signals that leak feelings without the person intending to send them
senses.definitionCN: 在本人无意发送时泄露情感的身体信号
senses.example: Researchers measured body language during the interviews.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者在访谈期间测量身体语言。
senses.why: Psychology treats much bodily signalling as automatic, which is why it can betray what speech conceals.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把许多身体信号视为自动发生，因此它能出卖言语所隐藏的东西。

senses.title: Animal posture signals
senses.definition: the postures and movements by which an animal signals mood or intention
senses.definitionCN: 动物用来表示情绪或意图的姿势与动作
senses.example: The dog's body language warned us to stay back.
senses.exampleCN: 那只狗的身体语言警告我们退后。
senses.why: The phrase extends beyond humans because animals also read stance, tail and distance as signals.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语扩展到人类之外，因为动物也把站姿、尾巴与距离读作信号。

senses.title: A skill taught in professional settings
senses.titleCN: 职业培训中教授的技能
senses.definition: the practical ability to read and control bodily signals in sales, negotiation or leadership
senses.definitionCN: 在销售、谈判或领导中读取与控制身体信号的实用能力
senses.example: The workshop taught body language for negotiations.
senses.exampleCN: 这场工作坊教授谈判中的身体语言。
senses.why: Once the signals are understood, they become a trainable skill rather than a mere fact of behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这些信号被理解，它们就成为可训练的技能，而不只是行为事实。

senses.title: Expressive physicality in performance
senses.titleCN: 表演中富有表现力的身体动作
senses.definition: the deliberate use of posture and movement by a performer to convey character or mood
senses.definitionCN: 表演者有意使用姿势与动作传达角色或情绪
senses.example: The dancer's body language filled the empty stage.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者的身体语言填满了空荡的舞台。
senses.why: Performance uses the same bodily code deliberately, turning everyday stance into expressive material.
senses.whyCN: 表演有意使用同一套身体代码，把日常站姿变成表现材料。

senses.title: Digital body language
senses.titleCN: 数字交流中的身体语言
senses.definition: the tone, timing, punctuation and emoji that stand in for bodily signals in text
senses.definitionCN: 在文字交流中替代身体信号的语气、时机、标点与表情符号
senses.example: Emoji and punctuation form a kind of digital body language.
senses.exampleCN: 表情符号与标点构成一种数字身体语言。
senses.why: When bodies are absent, writers rebuild the missing signals with marks on a screen.
senses.whyCN: 当身体不在场时，写作者用屏幕上的符号重建缺失的信号。

intro.en: Body language is an English compound of body, from Old English bodig, and language, from Latin lingua 'tongue' through Old French. The phrase is a modern coinage. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: body language 是英语合成词，由源自古英语 bodig 的 body 与经古法语来自拉丁语 lingua「舌头」的 language 组成。这个短语是近代新造。年代均为约数。

items.en: Bodig meant the physical frame of a person or animal; its further origin is obscure and not settled.
items.cn: bodig 指人或动物的身体骨架；其更早来源模糊，没有定论。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue, language'. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and the forms proposed for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: lingua 意为「舌头、语言」。其更深来源不确定，为它提出的形式属于重构。

items.en: Old French langage carried the word into English as language, first meaning the faculty of speech and then a system of signs.
items.cn: 古法语 langage 把这个词带入英语成为 language，最初指说话能力，后指符号系统。

items.en: The phrase body language is recorded in the early twentieth century and became widely popular with mid-century writing on nonverbal communication.
items.cn: body language 这一短语在二十世纪初见于记录，并随二十世纪中叶关于非言语交流的写作而广泛流行。

items.en: Later it became a practical label in sales, negotiation and leadership training, where reading stance was treated as a skill.
items.cn: 后来它成为销售、谈判与领导力培训中的实用标签，读懂姿势被视为一种技能。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first citation of the compound is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of lingua remains unsettled, so proposed forms are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个合成词确切的最早书证没有定论，lingua 在拉丁语之前的来源也未确定，提出的形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds compounds and technical terms that look close but name different things; group two holds near synonyms for wordless signalling.
note.cn: 第一组是外形接近却指不同事物的合成词与术语；第二组是表示无词信号的近义词。

entries.definition: It names the internal rhythm that regulates sleep and hunger, not a system of signals.
entries.definitionCN: 命名调节睡眠与饥饿的内部节律，而不是信号系统。

entries.definition: A political metaphor for a nation as an organized whole; the body here is figurative and not communicative.
entries.definitionCN: 把国家比作有组织的整体的政治隐喻；这里的身体是比喻性的，并不传达信息。

entries.definition: A full language with grammar and vocabulary made of hand and body signs; body language is unsystematic and not a language in that sense.
entries.definitionCN: 由手与身体符号构成、具备语法与词汇的完整语言；body language 不系统，也不是那个意义上的语言。

entries.definition: It names tone, pace and volume that accompany speech; body language excludes the voice.
entries.definitionCN: 指伴随言语的语调、语速与音量；body language 不包括嗓音。

entries.definition: The academic study of bodily movement as communication; the compound is the everyday name for the behaviour studied.
entries.definitionCN: 研究身体动作作为交流的学术领域；这个合成词是该行为的日常名称。

entries.definition: Only the arrangement of the body while standing or sitting; body language includes movement, spacing and touch as well.
entries.definitionCN: 只指站立或坐着时身体的排列；body language 还包括动作、距离与触碰。

entries.definition: The academic term for all wordless signalling, including tone and images; body language is the bodily part.
entries.definitionCN: 指所有无词信号的学术术语，包括语调与图像；body language 是其中身体的部分。

entries.definition: A person's overall manner and bearing, which may suggest character; body language focuses on signals and their reading.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的整体举止与风度，可暗示性格；body language 聚焦于信号及其解读。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two parts of the compound, the main channels and the technical contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：合成词的两个部分、主要渠道与技术对比。

normal.en: The compound says the body behaves like a language: signals, patterns, reading.
normal.cn: 这个合成词说身体像一种语言：有信号、模式与解读。

normal.en: Main channels: posture, hand movement, eye contact, spacing and touch.
normal.cn: 主要渠道：姿势、手部动作、眼神接触、距离与触碰。

normal.en: Contrast pair: body language is bodily, while paralanguage is vocal but still wordless.
normal.cn: 对比配对：body language 是身体的，而副语言是嗓音的、同样无词的。

normal.en: Professional use: sales and negotiation training treats it as a readable skill.
normal.cn: 职业用法：销售与谈判培训把它当作可解读的技能。

normal.en: Modern extension: emoji and punctuation are called digital body language.
normal.cn: 现代延伸：表情符号与标点被称为数字身体语言。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing still, yet saying a whole paragraph by stance alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人一动不动，却只靠站姿就说出一整段话。

abstract.en: Picture a dog lowering its head before any sound is made.
abstract.cn: 想象一只狗在发出任何声音之前先低下头。

abstract.en: Picture a text message whose punctuation does the work of a raised eyebrow.
abstract.cn: 想象一条短信，靠标点做出扬眉的动作。

examples.en: Her crossed arms were read as defensive body language.
examples.cn: 她交叉的双臂被读作防御性的身体语言。

examples.en: The trainer asked the class to notice body language during interviews.
examples.cn: 培训师让学员留意面试中的身体语言。

examples.en: In some cultures, the same body language is considered polite rather than rude.
examples.cn: 在某些文化里，同样的身体语言被视为礼貌而非粗鲁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「身体」加「语言」——身体不用嘴也在说话 → 身体语言

root: 英语合成词：body 源自古英语 bodig「身体」，language 经古法语来自拉丁语 lingua「舌头、语言」。短语为近代新造；两词的更深来源均有不确定处。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the general system to one person's posture, cultural codes, unconscious cues, animal signals, trained skill, stage expression and the digital substitute.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般系统，走到一个人的姿势、文化代码、无意识线索、动物信号、受训技能、舞台表达与数字替代物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a standing body that forms a sentence without opening its mouth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个站着的身体不张嘴就组成了一句话。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND ONE BODY: the general code and a single person's present stance are the same signals at two scales.
branches.cn: 系统与单个身体：一般代码与一个人当下的站姿，是同一套信号的两个尺度。

branches.en: CULTURE: the same stance can carry different meanings in different communities.
branches.cn: 文化：同样的站姿在不同群体中可携带不同意义。

branches.en: READING AND TRAINING: unconscious cues can be measured, and then taught as a practical skill.
branches.cn: 解读与训练：无意识线索可以被测量，然后作为实用技能被教授。

branches.en: ANIMAL: posture and distance signal mood beyond the human case.
branches.cn: 动物：姿势与距离在人类之外也传达情绪。

branches.en: STAGE AND SCREEN: performers use the code deliberately, and writers rebuild it with punctuation and emoji.
branches.cn: 舞台与屏幕：表演者有意使用这套代码，写作者则用标点与表情符号重建它。

intro.en: Body language is a two-word compound; each half has its own history, and the pair became a fixed label for wordless signalling.
intro.cn: body language 是一个两词合成短语；两半各有自己的历史，合在一起成为无词信号的固定标签。

latinIntro.en: English body comes from Old English bodig, while language comes from Latin lingua 'tongue' through Old French; the compound itself is modern English.
latinIntro.cn: 英语 body 源自古英语 bodig，而 language 经古法语来自拉丁语 lingua「舌头」；合成短语本身是近代英语。

items.example: The body carries signals before speech begins.
items.exampleCN: 身体在言语开始之前就携带信号。

items.example: The Latin noun named both the organ and the faculty.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词既指器官，也指能力。

items.example: The suffix helped form language from the French verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀帮助从法语动词构成表示「语言」的词。

items.example: The phrase borrows the word language for the body.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语把「语言」一词借给了身体。
身体语言影响了那场面试。

items.meaningCN: 作定语放在另一名词前
items.example: Body-language research grew after the war.
items.exampleCN: 身体语言研究在战后发展起来。

items.example: A tilted head is a body language cue.
items.exampleCN: 歪头是一个身体语言线索。

items.meaning: a person who reads such signals professionally
items.meaningCN: 以解读这类信号为职业的人
items.example: The body language expert warned against overreading.
items.exampleCN: 这位身体语言专家提醒不要过度解读。

definition_zh: 土著的；原住民的；土生的；原始的
definition_en: belonging to the people or species that were present in a place from the earliest times
core_image: 从土地最深处长出来的第一代人，脚与泥土连在一起
scene: 博物馆的展柜里摆着世代居住在河谷的人使用过的工具。 The exhibition honours the aboriginal people of the river valley.
sceneCN: 这里 aboriginal 是「原住民的」（第 1 个义项：最早居住在某地的人群）；句意为展览致敬河谷的原住民。

pos.zh: 土著的；原住民的
原住民；土著居民

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉形容词后缀构成，义为「原住民；土著居民」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「最初地；原初地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「原初性；本土性」

senses.title: Of a land's first peoples
senses.definition: belonging to the peoples who lived in a region before others arrived
senses.definitionCN: 属于在其他群体到来之前就居住于某地的人群
senses.example: The museum works with aboriginal communities.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆与原住民社群合作。
senses.why: Latin ab origine means 'from the beginning'; the people who were there from the beginning are named by that phrase.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ab origine 意为「从最初开始」；从一开始就在那里的人，正是由这个短语命名的。

senses.title: Native to a region
senses.definition: of a plant or animal, native to a place rather than introduced
senses.definitionCN: 指动植物原产于某地，而非外来引入
senses.example: The park protects several aboriginal species.
senses.exampleCN: 这座公园保护着几种本土物种。
senses.why: The 'from the beginning' idea applies to living things as well: a species that was there first is aboriginal to the land.
senses.whyCN: 「从最初开始」的观念也适用于生物：最早就在那里的物种，对这片土地而言就是土生的。

senses.title: Original and earliest
senses.definition: existing from the earliest period, before later changes
senses.definitionCN: 存在于最早时期、早于后来变化的
senses.example: The study traces aboriginal forms of the language.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究追溯这种语言最早的形式。
senses.why: Anything that dates from the beginning can be called aboriginal, including ideas and language forms.
senses.whyCN: 任何始于最初的事物都可称为 aboriginal，包括观念与语言形式。

senses.title: Of Aboriginal Australia
senses.definition: relating to the Indigenous peoples of Australia
senses.definitionCN: 与澳大利亚原住民族群有关的
senses.example: She studies aboriginal art from the north.
senses.exampleCN: 她研究北部的原住民艺术。
senses.why: In Australian English the capitalized Aboriginal is the standard term for the continent's first peoples.
senses.whyCN: 在澳大利亚英语中，大写的 Aboriginal 是称呼该大陆最早居民的通用术语。

senses.title: Of a native culture
senses.definition: belonging to the culture of a place's first inhabitants
senses.definitionCN: 属于某地最早居民的文化
senses.example: The festival celebrates aboriginal traditions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日庆祝原住民传统。
senses.why: Culture is one of the things a first people carries, so the adjective naturally attaches to its songs, stories, and rites.
senses.whyCN: 文化是原住民族所承载的事物之一，因此这个形容词自然附着于他们的歌谣、故事与仪式。

senses.title: Growing in its native range
senses.definition: growing naturally in the area where it evolved
senses.definitionCN: 在它演化所在的地区自然生长
senses.example: These aboriginal grasses survive long droughts.
senses.exampleCN: 这些原生草种能挺过漫长干旱。
senses.why: A plant that has always grown in a region is a first inhabitant of that soil, and the word borrows the human image.
senses.whyCN: 一直在某地生长的植物，是那片土壤最早的居民，这个词借用了人的意象。

senses.title: Inherited from early ancestors
senses.definition: coming from the earliest ancestors of a group
senses.definitionCN: 来自某个群体最早的祖先
