senses.example: The elders keep aboriginal knowledge of the seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 长者们保存着祖先传下的季节知识。
senses.why: Knowledge that passes from the first inhabitants is treated as part of the same inheritance.
senses.whyCN: 从最早居民传下来的知识，被视为同一份遗产的一部分。

senses.title: Untouched and original
senses.definition: describing a landscape or condition before outside change
senses.definitionCN: 形容在外部改变之前的地貌或状态
senses.example: The valley remains in its aboriginal state.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷仍保持原始状态。
senses.why: Landscapes untouched by later settlement are imagined as still standing at the beginning.
senses.whyCN: 未被后来定居改变的地貌，被想象成仍停在最初的样子。

intro.en: Aboriginal is built directly from a Latin phrase meaning 'from the beginning', and it preserves that phrase almost transparently.
intro.cn: aboriginal 直接由意为「从最初开始」的拉丁短语构成，几乎透明地保留了那个短语。

items.en: ab is a Latin preposition meaning 'from, away from'.
items.cn: ab 是拉丁语介词，意为「从、离开」。

items.en: origo meant 'a beginning, source, birth'; it also produced origin and original.
items.cn: origo 意为「开端、源头、出生」，也衍生出 origin 与 original。

items.en: The phrase ab origine, 'from the beginning', was used of peoples and things present from the first.
items.cn: 短语 ab origine 意为「从最初开始」，用于从一开始就存在的人群与事物。

items.en: The plural Aborigines named the first inhabitants of a region in Roman writing.
items.cn: 复数 Aborigines 在罗马文献中指某地最早的居民。

items.en: English aboriginal appears in the seventeenth century as an adjective for the earliest inhabitants.
items.cn: 英语 aboriginal 在十七世纪出现，作形容词指最早的居民。

items.en: The term spread to botany, geology, and Australian usage, where Aboriginal names the continent's first peoples.
items.cn: 这个术语扩展到植物学、地质学与澳大利亚用法；在那里，Aboriginal 指该大陆最早的居民。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adverb, and related origin words; the second gathers adjectives for what was there first.
note.cn: 第一组收名词、副词与相关的「起源」词；第二组收表示「最早就在那里」的形容词。

entries.definition: A member of the first people of a region; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「原住民、土著居民」，是形容词背后的名词形式。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'from the beginning or in the original state'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「最初地、原初地」。

entries.definition: The quality of being original to a place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「原初性、本土性」，指属于某地原初事物的性质。

entries.definition: The point where something begins; from the same Latin noun origo.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「起源」，来自同一个拉丁名词 origo。

entries.definition: Born or growing naturally in a particular place.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「土生土长的、原产的」，指在某地自然出生或生长。

entries.definition: Belonging to a place by birth or natural growth.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「本地的、天生的」，指因出生或自然生长而属于某地。

entries.definition: Existing from the start, before copies or changes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最初的、原来的」，指在复制或改变之前就存在。

entries.definition: Belonging to an early stage of development.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「原始的」，指属于发展的早期阶段。

entries.definition: Coming before all others in time or order.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最早的、第一的」，在时间或顺序上先于其他。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks work from the Latin phrase ab origine and the common policy collocations; the abstract hooks picture the first feet on the land.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点来自拉丁短语 ab origine 与常见政策搭配；抽象记忆点想象最早踏上这片土地的脚。

normal.en: Aboriginal is literally ab origine, 'from the beginning'.
normal.cn: aboriginal 字面就是 ab origine，即「从最初开始」。

normal.en: Aboriginal people and aboriginal rights are standard public-policy phrases.
normal.cn: aboriginal people 与 aboriginal rights 是标准公共政策短语。

normal.en: Origin, original, and aboriginal all share the Latin noun origo.
normal.cn: origin、original 与 aboriginal 都共享拉丁名词 origo。

normal.en: In Australian English, Aboriginal with a capital letter names the continent's first peoples.
normal.cn: 在澳大利亚英语中，大写的 Aboriginal 指该大陆最早的居民。

normal.en: The adjective also works for plants and landscapes that were there first.
normal.cn: 这个形容词也适用于最早就在那里的植物与地貌。

abstract.en: Picture bare feet pressing into soil that no one else has walked on.
abstract.cn: 想象赤脚踩进无人走过的泥土。

abstract.en: Picture a seed already in the ground before any fence is built.
abstract.cn: 想象围栏尚未建起，种子早已在土里。

abstract.en: Picture a hand painting the same pattern that ancestors painted on rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手画出祖先曾画在岩石上的同一个图案。

examples.en: The law recognizes aboriginal land rights.
examples.cn: 法律承认原住民的土地权利。

examples.en: Several aboriginal languages are endangered.
examples.cn: 几种原住民语言濒临消亡。

examples.en: The valley still holds aboriginal forest.
examples.cn: 这个山谷仍保有原始森林。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿伯瑞金诺」——阿伯一出生就在这片土地上，脚底沾着最原始的泥。

root: 拉丁语 ab（从）+ origo（起源），短语 ab origine 意为「从最初开始」；核心义是「从一开始就在某地」

sensesIntro.en: The senses start with the first peoples, then extend to native species, earliest forms, Australian usage, culture, plants, inherited knowledge, and untouched landscapes.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从最早的居民开始，扩展到本土物种、最早形式、澳大利亚用法、文化、植物、祖传知识与未开发的地貌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first feet standing on untouched ground
core.cn: 核心意象：最早踏上未动过的土地的双脚

branches.en: Human first peoples, including the capitalized Australian term.
branches.cn: 人类中最早的居民，包括澳大利亚的大写用法。

branches.en: Plants and animals native to a place from the start.
branches.cn: 从一开始就原产于某地的动植物。

branches.en: Earliest forms of language and knowledge passed down.
branches.cn: 传下来的最早语言形式与知识。

branches.en: The culture carried by a place's first inhabitants.
branches.cn: 某地最早居民所承载的文化。

branches.en: Landscapes still in their original, unchanged state.
branches.cn: 仍保持原初、未被改变的地貌。

intro.en: The word is transparently built from the Latin preposition ab and the noun origo, with the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁介词 ab、名词 origo 与形容词后缀 -al 透明地构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin origo and ab origine are the direct source of the English word, so the Latin entries record the phrase and its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 origo 与短语 ab origine 是英语词的直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录这个短语及其名词。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「原住民；土著居民」
副词，义为「最初地；原初地」

definition_zh: 伪装；使动物、装备或人不易被发现的体色、形态或掩饰手段
definition_en: the colors, shapes or devices that make an animal, person or object hard to see or detect
core_image: 一只蛾的翅纹与树皮纹理完全重合，停上去就消失不见
scene: 树干上的蛾子把翅膀张开，翅面的斑纹与地衣的碎块几乎重合，寻找它的鸟从旁边飞过。 The moth spreads its wings against the trunk until the patches match the lichen, and the bird hunting it passes by, a textbook example of camouflage.
sceneCN: 这里 camouflage 指「使动物不易被发现的体色与斑纹」（第 1 个义项：外形与背景融为一体）；句意为蛾子的翅纹与地衣几乎重合，捕食的鸟从旁边飞过也没发现它。图中可辨识物件：树干、地衣、展开翅膀的蛾、飞过的鸟。

pos.zh: 伪装；保护色；掩饰手段（不可数）
伪装；掩饰

senses.title: Animal protective coloration
senses.definition: the colors and patterns that let an animal blend into its background
senses.definitionCN: 使动物与背景融为一体、难以被看见的颜色与图案
senses.example: The moth's wing patches match the lichen exactly.
senses.exampleCN: 蛾翅上的斑块与地衣完全相合。
senses.why: the word first served hunters and naturalists describing animals that seem to vanish against bark, sand or leaves.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初服务于猎人与博物学者，用来描述在树皮、沙地或叶片前仿佛消失的动物。

senses.title: Concealment by behavior
senses.definition: actions such as freezing, crouching or changing posture that reduce visibility
senses.definitionCN: 静止、伏低或改变姿态等降低可见度的动作
senses.example: The fawn lies flat and does not move while the doe feeds.
senses.exampleCN: 母鹿觅食时，幼鹿趴平不动。
senses.why: camouflage is not only worn; it is also done, and stillness can hide an animal whose colors already match.
senses.whyCN: 伪装不只穿在身上，也做在动作里；静止能藏住一只颜色已相配的动物。

senses.title: Military camouflage
senses.definition: the disguising of troops, vehicles and positions to avoid detection
senses.definitionCN: 使部队、车辆与阵地不被发现而进行的掩饰
senses.example: The battery was hidden under camouflage netting.
senses.exampleCN: 炮兵连被伪装网遮住。
senses.why: modern warfare made the word famous: a gun that can be seen is a gun that will be hit.
senses.whyCN: 现代战争让这个词广为人知：能被看见的火炮，就是会被击中的火炮。

senses.title: Camouflage clothing and material
senses.definition: the printed fabrics, nets and covers used to hide people or equipment
senses.definitionCN: 用于隐藏人员或装备的印花布料、网与遮盖物
senses.example: The unit wore woodland camouflage in the forest.
senses.exampleCN: 这支部队在森林里穿林地迷彩。
senses.why: metonymy turns the method into the kit: the pattern itself comes to be called camouflage.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把方法变成装备：图案本身也被称作 camouflage。

senses.title: Figurative disguise of intent
senses.definition: words or actions that hide one's real purpose or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 掩盖真实目的或感受的言语与行动
senses.example: His calm tone was camouflage for panic.
senses.exampleCN: 他平静的语气是对慌乱的掩饰。
senses.why: if a body can be hidden against a background, a motive can be hidden behind a manner.
senses.whyCN: 如果身体能藏在背景前，动机也能藏在举止后面。

senses.title: Protective coloration as a term
senses.definition: the biological term for coloration that lowers the chance of detection by predators or prey
senses.definitionCN: 指降低被天敌或猎物发现几率的体色的生物学术语
senses.example: Protective coloration is the scientific name for one kind of camouflage.
senses.exampleCN: 保护色是某一类伪装在科学上的名称。
senses.why: science needed a narrower label, so camouflage became the umbrella and protective coloration one branch under it.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要更窄的标签，于是 camouflage 成为伞名，保护色成为其下的一支。

senses.title: Resemblance to another object
senses.titleCN: 与另一物体相似的伪装形态
senses.definition: shapes that make an organism resemble a leaf, twig, stone or another species
senses.definitionCN: 使生物看起来像叶片、枝条、石头或另一物种的形态
senses.example: The insect's body mimics a dead twig.
senses.exampleCN: 这只昆虫的身体模仿一根枯枝。
senses.why: blending in and looking like something else are neighboring strategies, and everyday usage often puts both under camouflage.
senses.whyCN: 融入背景与长得像别的东西是相邻的策略，日常用法常把两者都归入 camouflage。

senses.title: Visual deception in design
senses.definition: the use of pattern and contrast to hide an object in plain sight, as in vehicles or buildings
senses.definitionCN: 用图案与对比把物体藏在显眼处，如车辆或建筑
senses.example: The aircraft's paint breaks up its outline against the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机的涂装打散了它在天空中的轮廓。
senses.why: the principle is general: high-contrast false edges defeat the eye that looks for a continuous outline.
senses.whyCN: 原理是通用的：高对比的假边缘能骗过寻找连续轮廓的眼睛。

intro.en: Camouflage came into English from French during the First World War; French camoufler 'to disguise' probably goes back to Italian camuffare, whose deeper origin is uncertain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: camouflage 在第一次世界大战期间由法语进入英语；法语 camoufler「伪装」大概可追溯到意大利语 camuffare，其更早来源不确定。年代为约数。

items.en: Camoufler meant 'to disguise, mask'; it was the verb used by French forces for hiding guns and positions from aerial observation.
items.cn: camoufler 意为「伪装、遮掩」；法国军队用它指把火炮与阵地隐藏起来，避开空中观察。

items.en: Italian camuffare 'to disguise, trick' is the likely source of the French verb; the two languages shared the term in military and theatrical circles.
items.cn: 意大利语 camuffare「伪装、欺骗」是法语动词的可能来源；两种语言在军事与戏剧圈中共用这个词。

items.en: Source uncertain: camuffare may involve capo 'head' plus muffare 'to muffle', but this is a suggestion, not an established derivation, and no reliable Latin root can be asserted.
items.cn: 来源不确定：camuffare 可能由 capo「头」与 muffare「包裹、闷住」组成，但这只是推测，并非确立的派生；无法断言可靠的拉丁词根。

items.en: English adopted camouflage during the First World War, first for the disguising of artillery and later for the painted patterns themselves.
items.cn: 英语在第一次世界大战期间借入 camouflage，最初指火炮的掩饰，后来指涂装图案本身。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word spread to animal coloration, hunting gear, fashion and figurative disguise of intention.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词扩展到动物体色、狩猎装备、时装，以及比喻性的意图掩饰。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on camouflage itself; group two holds neighboring strategies of concealment and imitation.
note.cn: 第一组是 camouflage 本身构成的形式；第二组是相邻的隐蔽与模仿策略。

entries.definition: Hidden by camouflage; the -ed form describes the object, while camouflage names the method or material.
entries.definitionCN: 被伪装遮住的；-ed 形式描述对象，而 camouflage 命名方法或材料。

entries.definition: A person who designs or applies camouflage, especially in the military; the French agent noun is rare in English.
entries.definitionCN: 设计或实施伪装的人，尤指军中；这个法语施动名词在英语中罕用。

entries.definition: A net printed or scrimmed to hide equipment; the compound narrows camouflage to one piece of kit.
entries.definitionCN: 用于遮盖装备的印花或网眼织物；该复合词把 camouflage 收窄为一件装备。

entries.definition: The informal short form for camouflage pattern or clothing; it has lost the final syllables and most of the formal tone.
entries.definitionCN: 伪装图案或服装的口语简称；省去末尾音节，也去掉了大部分正式语气。

entries.definition: The evolved resemblance of one organism to another; camouflage hides an animal in its background, mimicry makes it look like something else.
entries.definitionCN: 一种生物与另一种生物的演化相似；camouflage 把动物藏进背景，mimicry 让它看起来像别的东西。

entries.definition: A change of appearance meant to deceive; camouflage is one means of disguise, especially in the visual field.
entries.definitionCN: 为欺骗而改变外观；camouflage 是伪装的一种手段，尤在视觉层面。

entries.definition: The act of keeping something out of sight; it is the general purpose that camouflage serves.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物藏在视线之外的行为；是 camouflage 所服务的一般目的。

entries.definition: Coloration that reduces detection; it is the scientific term for one kind of camouflage.
entries.definitionCN: 降低被发现几率的体色；是某一类伪装在科学上的名称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is French military vocabulary adopted in 1917: first the act of masking guns, then the painted pattern.
normal.cn: 这个词是 1917 年借入的法语军事词汇：先指遮蔽火炮的动作，后指涂装图案。

normal.en: The family runs camouflage, camouflaged, camouflaging, camoufleur and the clipping camo.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 camouflage、camouflaged、camouflaging、camoufleur 与缩略 camo。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: natural camouflage, military camouflage, camouflage pattern, camouflage net.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：天然伪装、军事伪装、伪装图案、伪装网。

normal.en: Camouflage hides by matching the background; mimicry hides by resembling another object or species.
normal.cn: camouflage 靠与背景相合来隐藏；mimicry 靠像另一物体或物种来隐藏。

normal.en: Do not assert a Latin root: the deeper origin of camuffare is uncertain.
normal.cn: 不要断言拉丁词根：camuffare 的更早来源不确定。

abstract.en: Picture a moth whose wings are a copy of the bark it rests on.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蛾，翅膀就是它所停树皮的复制品。

abstract.en: Picture a net painted with the same shadows as the ground it covers.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网，画着与所盖地面相同的阴影。

abstract.en: Picture a calm face that hides a racing pulse.
abstract.cn: 想象一张平静的脸，藏住飞快的脉搏。

examples.en: The lizard's camouflage makes it almost invisible on the sand.
examples.cn: 蜥蜴的伪装让它在沙地上几乎看不见。

examples.en: Troops draped camouflage over the vehicles before dawn.
examples.cn: 部队在黎明前给车辆盖上伪装。

examples.en: His jokes were camouflage for a serious complaint.
examples.cn: 他的玩笑是对一项严肃抱怨的掩饰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡目弗拉日」——把身形卡进背景里，让目光滑过去 → 伪装

root: 法语 camouflage ← camoufler「伪装」← 意大利语 camuffare「伪装、欺骗」；更早来源不确定，无可靠拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from one trick: match the background, then hold still, then hide troops, wear the pattern, mask a motive, name the biological branch, resemble another object, and deceive the eye in design.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个把戏展开：与背景相合、保持不动、藏住部队、穿上图案、掩盖动机、命名生物学分支、像另一物体，以及在设计中骗过眼睛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an outline that stops being an outline because the surface behind it is repeated on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个轮廓不再是轮廓，因为它表面重复了背后的纹理。

branches.en: THE BIOLOGY: matching the background, naming the branch, and resembling another object are three related tricks.
branches.cn: 生物学：与背景相合、命名分支、像另一物体，是三个相关把戏。

branches.en: STILLNESS: behavior completes what coloration begins.
branches.cn: 静止：行为补全体色开始的事。

branches.en: THE MILITARY: the word's modern fame comes from hiding guns and then wearing the pattern.
branches.cn: 军事：这个词的现代名声来自藏炮，随后是穿上图案。

branches.en: HIDDEN MOTIVE: words and actions disguise what is really intended.
branches.cn: 隐藏的动机：言语与行动掩盖真实意图。

branches.en: DESIGN: false edges defeat the eye that searches for a continuous outline.
branches.cn: 设计：假边缘骗过寻找连续轮廓的眼睛。

intro.en: Camouflage is a French noun in -age built on the verb camoufler. English adds -ed, -ing and a clipping, but the deeper morphology is not reliably recoverable.
intro.cn: camouflage 是法语中以 -age 结尾的名词，由动词 camoufler 构成。英语加上 -ed、-ing 与一个缩略形式，但更早的形态无法可靠还原。

latinIntro.en: Camouflage has no reliable Latin cognate, so latinEntries is left empty; the likely Italian source camuffare is itself of uncertain origin.
latinIntro.cn: camouflage 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁词条留空；可能的意大利语来源 camuffare 本身来源不明。

items.example: French units camouflaged their guns in 1915.
items.exampleCN: 法军部队在 1915 年伪装火炮。

items.structure: Italian verb, probable source of camoufler
items.example: The Italian verb is the likely origin, not a proven one.
items.exampleCN: 这个意大利语动词是可能来源，而非已证来源。

items.meaning: an action or a collective result
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into the name of the practice.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成实践的名称。

items.meaning: the act or material of disguising
items.example: Camouflage hid the battery from the air.
items.exampleCN: 伪装把炮兵连从空中藏了起来。
一位伪装师设计了这些网。

items.example: He wore camo in the field.

items.meaning: a net used to hide equipment
items.example: They spread a camouflage net over the trench.
items.exampleCN: 他们在战壕上铺开伪装网。

items.meaningCN: 用于发现被伪装物体的方法
items.exampleCN: 热成像相机可作反伪装手段。

definition_zh: 工匠；手艺人；以手工小批量制作并留名于作品的匠人
definition_en: a skilled worker who makes things by hand, usually in small quantities
core_image: 一人一炉一案，面包在掌下成形，炉门上还留着手抹的泥
scene: 清晨的作坊里，面包师把面团从木盆取出，用手掌压出气孔，再送进砖炉。 An artisan marks each loaf with a small slash so buyers know whose hands made it.
sceneCN: 这里 artisan 指「以手工小批量制作、作品带个人印记的匠人」（第 6 个义项：以个人风格为标志的制作者）；句意为这位匠人在每条面包上划一道小口作记号，好让买者知道出自谁手。

pos.zh: 工匠；手艺人（可数；亦作定语，如「匠人面包」这一说法）

derivatives.zh: artisan + -al（形容词后缀）→ 手工制作的（语义偏移：从人转向产品属性）
artisan + -ship（状态）→ 匠人身份与技艺
拉丁 ars（技艺）→ 艺术（同根不同线，经古法语进入英语）
art + -ist（从事者）→ 艺术家（同根，但走的是 art 而非 artisan 这条线）
arte（技艺）+ factum（做成之物）→ 人工制品

senses.title: Skilled worker who makes by hand
senses.titleCN: 以手工制作的熟练工人
senses.definition: a person whose trade is shaping material with trained hands and tools
senses.definitionCN: 以受训的双手与工具加工材料为职业的人
senses.example: The bench was made by a local artisan from oak felled on the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 这条长凳由本地匠人用庄园里砍下的橡木制成。
senses.why: The word reaches English from Latin ars 'skill' through Italian and French, and it names the person who holds the skill rather than the skill.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经意大利语与法语从拉丁 ars「技艺」进入英语，指持有技艺的人，而不是技艺本身。

senses.title: Small-scale independent producer
senses.definition: a maker who works in a small workshop rather than a factory
senses.definitionCN: 在小作坊而非工厂里生产的制作者
senses.example: Artisans in the old quarter still sell directly from their workshops.
senses.exampleCN: 老城区的匠人至今仍在作坊门口直接售卖。
senses.why: A hand worker cannot scale like a plant, so the word carries a built-in contrast with industry.
senses.whyCN: 靠手的人无法像工厂那样扩产，因此这个词自带与工业相对的含义。

senses.title: Maker of one traditional product
senses.titleCN: 某一种传统产品的制作者
senses.definition: a maker of a particular regional good such as cheese, bread, tile or lacquer ware
senses.definitionCN: 制作某一地方性产品的人，如奶酪、面包、屋瓦或漆器
senses.example: The village artisans still fire roof tiles in a wood kiln.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的匠人仍用柴窑烧制屋瓦。
senses.why: Long practice in one product turns a general hand worker into the named maker of that product.
senses.whyCN: 长期只做一种产品，会让一般的手工者变成该产品的具名制作者。

senses.title: Guild master in a medieval town
senses.titleCN: 中世纪城镇中的行会匠师
senses.definition: in medieval towns, a master of a trade organized under a guild
senses.definitionCN: 在中世纪城镇里，隶属于行会的行业师傅
senses.example: Only artisans of the guild could sell silver within the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 只有行会中的匠人才能在城墙内出售银器。
senses.why: Guilds turned a personal skill into a licensed status, and artisan was the word for that status.
senses.whyCN: 行会把个人技艺变成受许可的身份，artisan 正是指这一身份的词。

senses.title: Worker who owns the tools
senses.definition: in economic writing, a producer who owns the means of production instead of selling only labour
senses.definitionCN: 在经济文献中，拥有生产资料而非仅出卖劳动力的生产者
senses.example: The study compares artisans who own their looms with workers who rent them.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究比较了自有织机的匠人与租用织机的工人。
senses.why: Ownership follows from small-scale work: the person who makes the whole thing usually owns the bench.
senses.whyCN: 所有权由小规模作业而来：做完整件东西的人通常拥有那张工作台。

senses.title: Maker whose work carries a name
senses.titleCN: 作品带个人署名的制作者
senses.definition: a maker valued because individual pieces can be traced to one pair of hands
senses.definitionCN: 因单件作品可追溯到某一双手而受重视的制作者
senses.example: Collectors now pay more for pieces by named artisans than for factory sets.
senses.exampleCN: 藏家如今为有名有姓的匠人之作付的钱，比工厂成套品更多。
senses.why: Where output is not uniform, the maker becomes a brand, and the word acquires a market meaning.
senses.whyCN: 当产出并不均一时，制作者就成了品牌，这个词也随之带上市场含义。

senses.title: Deliberate maker outside manual work
senses.titleCN: 非手工领域的刻意制作者
senses.definition: a person who builds something carefully, said figuratively of writers, cooks or programmers
senses.definitionCN: 精心构建某物的人，可喻指写作者、厨师或程序员
senses.example: He calls himself an artisan of small, exact sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 他自称是一个做短小而精确句子的人。
senses.why: If the essence is care plus a signature, the material can be words or code as easily as clay.
senses.whyCN: 若核心是用心加署名，那么材料换成文字或代码，与换成黏土并无不同。

senses.title: Attributive label for handmade goods
senses.titleCN: 标示手工制品的定语用法
senses.definition: used before a noun to mark a product as hand-made and small-batch
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，标示产品为手工、小批量制作
senses.example: Artisan bread costs more because it is shaped and timed by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 手工面包更贵，因为它的成形与发酵都靠人手掌控。
senses.why: A noun that names a maker can stand before another noun and act as a certificate of origin.
senses.whyCN: 一个指制作者的名词可以放在另一名词前，充当产地与工艺的证明。

intro.en: Artisan is a Latin word that travelled through Italian and French before reaching English, and it keeps the workshop in view where artist keeps the studio.
intro.cn: artisan 是一个经意大利语与法语辗转进入英语的拉丁词；它眼里是作坊，而 artist 眼里是画室。

items.en: Ars, genitive artis, meant 'skill, craft, art'. It is generally connected with a Latin root for 'fitting together', reconstructed as *ar-, but that root is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: ars（属格 artis）意为「技艺、手艺、艺术」。它一般与一个表「接合」的拉丁词根相联系，重构为 *ar-，但该词根是重构形式，并非有记录的形式。

items.en: Artitus 'skilled, trained in an art' is the adjective built on ars that supplies the medieval stem of the word.
items.cn: artitus「有技艺的、受过训练的」是建于 ars 之上的形容词，提供了这个词的中世纪词干。

items.en: Spoken Latin formed *artitianus 'one who works at a craft'; the suffix -ianus marks a person belonging to or practising something.
items.cn: 口语拉丁构成 *artitianus「从事某门手艺的人」；后缀 -ianus 标出属于或从事某事的人。

items.en: Italian artigiano names a craftsman or tradesman and is the immediate source of the French form.
items.cn: 意大利语 artigiano 指工匠或手艺人，是法语形式的直接来源。

items.en: French artisan entered English in the sixteenth century, bringing with it the small workshop and the guild rather than the fine-art studio.
items.cn: 法语 artisan 于十六世纪进入英语，带来的是小作坊与行会，而不是美术画室。

items.en: English keeps the handwork sense and later adds the marketing sense of small-batch goods; the shared Latin root with art and artist is real, but the words arrived by different routes.
items.cn: 英语保留了手工义，后来又添上小批量货品的市场义；它与 art、artist 共享拉丁词根，但三者是经不同路径进入英语的。

note.en: The first group holds near-identical shapes, including one famous false friend; the second holds true synonyms with different emphases.
note.cn: 第一组是外形极近的词，其中一个是有名的假朋友；第二组是侧重点不同的真同义词。

entries.definition: Nothing to do with skill: it describes a well whose water rises under its own pressure, from the old province name Artois.
entries.definitionCN: 与技艺无关：指水靠自身压力上升的自流井，来自旧地名阿图瓦。

entries.definition: A maker of art, formed on art rather than on artisan; the two words share ars but came by different routes.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术创作者，由 art 而非 artisan 构成；两词共享 ars，但路径不同。

entries.definition: The adjective from artisan, now used mostly on goods and methods: artisanal cheese, artisanal mining.
entries.definitionCN: artisan 的形容词形式，如今多用于货品与方法：手工奶酪、手工采矿。

entries.definition: Art plus a form of facere 'to make'; it means a clever trick rather than honest handwork.
entries.definitionCN: art 加 facere「做」的某种形式；指巧计，而非诚实的手工。

entries.definition: The English-born equivalent; it stresses trained skill, while artisan stresses the small workshop and the trade status.
entries.definitionCN: 本族语中的对应词，强调受训技艺，而 artisan 强调小作坊与行会身份。

entries.definition: Anyone who makes something, including machines and companies; artisan implies a person and a hand.
entries.definitionCN: 任何制作者，包括机器与公司；artisan 隐含「人」与「手」。

entries.definition: A skilled worker who also sells, often at a shop or on a round; artisan usually makes rather than serves customers.
entries.definitionCN: 既制作也售卖、常守店面或走街的熟练者；artisan 通常只做不服务于顾客。

entries.definition: A worker in metal by name; artisan is the general term that covers clay, wood, cloth and food as well.
entries.definitionCN: 名字即指金属加工者；artisan 是涵盖陶、木、布、食的通称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ars 'skill' + -anus 'person concerned with': the one concerned with a skill.
normal.cn: ars「技艺」+ -anus「与…相关的人」：与某门技艺相关的那个人。

normal.en: The family runs artisan, artisanal, artisanship, and on the other line art, artist, artistic.
normal.cn: 同族词有 artisan、artisanal、artisanship，另一条线是 art、artist、artistic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark small-batch goods: artisan bread, artisan cheese, artisan goods.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出小批量货品：手工面包、手工奶酪、手工艺品。

normal.en: The workshop, not the studio, separates artisan from artist.
normal.cn: 分开 artisan 与 artist 的，是作坊而不是画室。

normal.en: The false friend artesian describes water under pressure, and it comes from a place name, not from a skill.
normal.cn: 假朋友 artesian 讲的是受压的水，来自地名，与技艺无关。

abstract.en: Picture a single pair of hands in a shop so small that the door is the counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一间小到门口就是柜台、只有一双手在干的作坊。

abstract.en: Picture a loaf with a slash on top, the maker's name written in one stroke.
abstract.cn: 想象一条顶上划了一刀的面包，那一刀就是制作者的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a guild seal on a silver cup, turning skill into a legal right to sell.
abstract.cn: 想象银杯上的行会印记，把技艺变成售卖的合法权利。

examples.en: A retired engineer and a village artisan rebuilt the clock tower by hand.
examples.cn: 一位退休工程师和一位村里匠人用手工重修了钟楼。

examples.en: The shop sells only what its own artisans can finish in a week.
examples.cn: 这家店只卖自家匠人一周内能完成的东西。

examples.en: Tourism has turned cheese making from a farm task into a craft with named artisans.
examples.cn: 旅游业把做奶酪从农活变成了有具名匠人的手艺。

dict_mnemonic.text: art（技艺）+ isan（人）＝ 靠一门技艺吃饭的人；记「一双手、一间小作坊、一个名字」。

root: 拉丁 ars（属格 artis）「技艺、艺术」+ 晚期拉丁 -ianus（从事某业的人）→ 意大利 artigiano → 法语 artisan；ars 更早来源一般重构为 *ar-「接合」，属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a pair of hands to a market label: the hand worker, the small shop, the single product, the guild master, the owner of tools, the signed piece, the figurative maker, and the adjective on a loaf.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一双匠人的手出发走到一个市场标签：手工者、小作坊、单一产品、行会师傅、工具所有者、署名作品、比喻中的制作者，以及写在面包上的定语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one pair of hands, one bench, one product, and a mark that says who made it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手、一张工作台、一种产品，以及一个标明出自谁手的记号。

branches.en: FROM HAND TO SPECIALITY: general hand skill narrows into the named maker of one traditional good.
branches.cn: 从手到专精：一般的手工技艺收窄为某一传统产品的具名制作者。

branches.en: SMALL SCALE AS A LABEL: the workshop facts become a word placed on goods to certify origin.
branches.cn: 小规模成为标签：作坊里的事实变成一个放在货品上、用来证明来历的词。

branches.en: STATUS AND OWNERSHIP: the guild licenses the trade, and the small producer owns the bench.
branches.cn: 身份与所有权：行会给行业发许可，小生产者拥有那张工作台。

branches.en: SIGNATURE VALUE: when pieces differ, a name on the piece becomes the reason to pay more.
branches.cn: 署名价值：当每件作品并不相同时，作品上的名字就成了多付钱的理由。

branches.en: MATERIAL BECOMES OPTIONAL: if care and signature define the word, words and code qualify as much as clay.
branches.cn: 材料成为可选：若核心是用心与署名，文字与代码和黏土一样够格。

intro.en: Artisan is built from a Latin noun of skill plus a Latin person suffix, and both parts still build English words on their own.
intro.cn: artisan 由一个表技艺的拉丁名词加一个拉丁人称后缀构成，两部分至今都能独立构成英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars supplies art, artist, artistic, artifice and inert through related forms; the person suffix -ianus supplies artisan, and the same pattern gives Italian artigiano and French artisan.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ars 经由相关形式给出 art、artist、artistic、artifice 等词；人称后缀 -ianus 给出 artisan，同一模式也给出意大利语 artigiano 与法语 artisan。

items.example: The noun is the head of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个词族的源头。

items.example: The adjective supplies the medieval stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供了中世纪词干。

items.meaning: one who works at a craft
items.example: The spoken form is reconstructed from its descendants.
items.exampleCN: 这个口语形式是由其后续语言重构出来的。

items.structure: art (English noun from Latin ars through Old French)
items.example: The short noun keeps only the aesthetic branch.
items.exampleCN: 这个短名词只保留了审美那一支。

items.example: The studio word, not the workshop word.
items.exampleCN: 这是画室的词，不是作坊的词。

items.example: The suffix moves the word from person to product.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词从人移到产品。

items.example: The suffix abstracts the person into a condition.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把人抽象成一种状态。

items.example: The compound joins skill with making.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把技艺与制作连在一起。

items.example: The same skill is here turned toward deception.
items.exampleCN: 同样的技艺在此转向欺瞒。

definition_zh: adj. 爱发号施令的，专横的
definition_en: fond of telling other people what to do; trying to control a group even without authority
core_image: 游戏刚开场，最小的孩子就站到中间发号施令
scene: 游戏刚开始，最小的孩子就站到中间宣布了全部规则。 The game had barely begun when the youngest child started giving orders, and the others called her bossy.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bossy 指爱对别人发号施令；句意是游戏刚开始，最小的孩子就宣布全部规则，被人叫作专横。

pos.zh: 爱发号施令的；专横的

senses.title: Fond of giving orders
senses.definition: liking to tell other people what to do
senses.definitionCN: 喜欢吩咐别人做这做那
senses.example: Her bossy cousin decided where everyone would sit.
senses.exampleCN: 她那个专横的表姐决定每个人坐哪儿。
senses.why: Boss, borrowed from Dutch baas, plus -y meaning full of.
senses.whyCN: boss 借自荷兰语 baas，加 -y 表示「充满」。

senses.title: Domineering without authority
senses.definition: trying to control a group although holding no official power
senses.definitionCN: 虽无正式职权却试图控制一群人
senses.example: A bossy classmate can make group work miserable.
senses.exampleCN: 一个专横的同学能让小组作业变得难熬。
senses.why: The label is used most often of children, who hold no formal power.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最常用来评价孩子，而孩子并没有正式权力。

intro.en: Bossy adds -y to boss, an American borrowing of Dutch baas, a master.
intro.cn: bossy 是 boss 加 -y；boss 是美式英语从荷兰语 baas（主人）借来的词。

items.en: Baas means a master or an employer.
items.cn: baas 意为主人或雇主。

items.en: American English borrows boss as a title.
items.cn: 美式英语借入 boss 作称谓。

items.en: Bossy names a person fond of ordering others.
items.cn: bossy 指爱指挥他人的人。

items.en: The label is used mostly of children.
items.cn: 该词多用于评价孩子。

items.en: Bossy describes a style of leading badly.
items.cn: bossy 描述一种糟糕的领导风格。

items.en: Bossy is often paired with confident.
items.cn: 现代常把 bossy 与自信并提。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ossy shape; the near-meaning group moves from mild pushiness to open dictatorship.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ossy 形状；近义组从轻微的强推排到公开的专断。

entries.definition: An employer, or to give orders.
entries.definitionCN: 雇主；发号施令。

entries.definition: Covered with moss.
entries.definitionCN: 长满苔藓的。

entries.definition: Shiny and smooth.
entries.definitionCN: 光亮平滑的。

entries.definition: Losing data when compressed.
entries.definitionCN: 压缩时丢失数据的。

entries.definition: Too eager to get what you want.
entries.definitionCN: 过于急切地想得到想要的。

entries.definition: Trying to control others in an arrogant way.
entries.definitionCN: 傲慢地试图控制他人。

entries.definition: Treating others as if they must obey.
entries.definitionCN: 把别人当作必须服从的人。

entries.definition: Acting like a ruler who tolerates no dissent.
entries.definitionCN: 像不容异议的统治者那样行事。

normalIntro.en: A bossy person carries a boss around in their voice.
normalIntro.cn: 专横的人嗓子里总带着一个「老板」。

normal.en: Boss is the person who gives orders.
normal.cn: boss 是发号施令的那个人。

normal.en: -y turns the noun into a trait.
normal.cn: -y 把这个名词变成一种性格。

normal.en: Bossy means full of boss, with no rank to back it.
normal.cn: bossy 意为「满是老板气」，却并无职位支撑。

normal.en: It is most often said of children.
normal.cn: 这个词最常用来形容孩子。

normal.en: The tone, not the job title, is what people hear.
normal.cn: 人们听到的是口吻，而不是职位。

abstract.en: A small general with no army.
abstract.cn: 一个没有军队的小将军。

abstract.en: Orders handed out like sweets.
abstract.cn: 像发糖一样发号施令。

abstract.en: A voice that fills a room.
abstract.cn: 撑满整个房间的一个声音。

examples.en: The bossy child told the others where to stand.
examples.cn: 那个爱指挥的孩子告诉大家站在哪儿。

examples.en: He was bossy about the rules but never about the work.
examples.cn: 他对规则很专横，却从不掺和工作本身。

examples.en: Teachers now avoid calling a girl bossy for leading.
examples.cn: 如今老师避免因为女孩带头就称她专横。

dict_mnemonic.text: boss（老板）+ -y（充满……的）——满身老板气，爱指挥人。

root: boss（老板）+ -y（有……性质的）

sensesIntro.en: Bossy is about the sound of an order, not the right to give it.
sensesIntro.cn: bossy 说的是命令的口吻，而不是下命令的权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the smallest child standing in the middle, handing out the rules
core.cn: 核心意象：最小的孩子站在中间，把规则一条条发下去

branches.en: A cousin assigning everyone a seat.
branches.cn: 给每个人指定座位的表姐。

branches.en: A tone that sounds like a manager.
branches.cn: 听起来像经理的口吻。

branches.en: A classmate rewriting the group plan.
branches.cn: 重写小组计划的同学。

branches.en: A child with no rank and a full agenda.
branches.cn: 没有职位却议程满满的孩子。

branches.en: Authority borrowed by volume.
branches.cn: 靠音量借来的权威。

intro.en: Bossy is boss plus -y; the list below covers it and the vocabulary of command.
intro.cn: bossy 是 boss 加 -y；下面列出它以及「命令」词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin dominus is a master, and imperare is to command.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dominus 意为主人，imperare 意为命令。

latinEntries.exampleCN: dominus 产生 dominate 与 domineer。

definition_zh: 选举的；选举人的；与选民有关的
definition_en: relating to elections, to electors or to the system by which votes are counted
core_image: 一张被划成许多格子的地图，每格上写着数字，数字加起来等于一个总数
scene: 墙上挂着一张被划成许多格子的地图，每格都写着数字。 The electoral system gives small districts more weight than their population.
sceneCN: 句中这个词指与选举制度有关的（第 3 个义项：关于选票如何计算的制度安排）；句意为这套选举制度让小选区获得超过其人口比例的权重。图中可辨识物件：分格地图、数字牌、计票表、选区边界线、投票箱。

pos.zh: 选举的；与选举有关的
选举人的；与选民有关的

senses.title: Relating to elections
senses.definition: concerning the process or event of voting people into office
senses.definitionCN: 与把人员投票选入公职的程序或活动有关的
senses.example: Electoral reform dominated the party's manifesto.
senses.exampleCN: 选举改革主导了该党的宣言。
senses.why: The adjective is elector plus -al, so it began as 'of the elector' and widened to the whole process.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词是 elector 加 -al，最初指「选民的」，后扩展到整个程序。

senses.title: Relating to voters
senses.definition: concerning the people who have the right to vote
senses.definitionCN: 与拥有投票权的人有关的
senses.example: The electoral roll was checked for duplicate names.
senses.exampleCN: 选民名册被核查是否有重名。
senses.why: An election exists only if there are electors, so the adjective often points at them directly.
senses.whyCN: 只有存在选民才有选举，因此这个形容词常常直接指向他们。

senses.title: Of a voting system
senses.definition: describing the rules that convert votes into seats, such as first-past-the-post or proportional representation
senses.definitionCN: 描述把选票换算成席位的规则，如简单多数制或比例代表制
senses.example: The electoral system gives small districts more weight than their population.
senses.exampleCN: 这套选举制度让小选区获得超过其人口比例的权重。
senses.why: How votes become seats is a separate machinery, and the adjective names that machinery.
senses.whyCN: 选票如何变成席位是一套独立的机器，这个形容词命名那套机器。

senses.title: Of districts and boundaries
senses.definition: relating to the geographic units that return members and the lines drawn around them
senses.definitionCN: 与推举议员的地理单位及其划界有关的
senses.example: The electoral boundary ran along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 选区边界沿河而行。
senses.why: Votes are counted by area in most systems, so the adjective attaches to maps.
senses.whyCN: 多数制度按地域计票，因此这个形容词附着在地图上。

senses.title: Of fraud and malpractice
senses.definition: used of illegal interference with voting, such as bribery or ballot tampering
senses.definitionCN: 用于指对投票的非法干预，如贿选或篡改选票
senses.example: The court annulled the result for electoral fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 法院因选举舞弊宣布结果无效。
senses.why: A process that distributes power attracts attempts to bend it, and the adjective marks those attempts.
senses.whyCN: 分配权力的程序会招来扭曲它的企图，这个形容词标记这类企图。

senses.title: Of electoral votes
senses.definition: relating to the votes cast by electors in an indirect system such as the American college
senses.definitionCN: 与间接制度（如美国选举人团）中选举人所投票数有关
senses.example: He won the electoral vote but lost the popular vote.
senses.exampleCN: 他赢下了选举人票，却输掉了普选票。
senses.why: In an indirect system, the elector is the voter, and the adjective distinguishes that layer from the public vote.
senses.whyCN: 在间接制度里，选举人就是投票者，这个形容词把这一层与公众投票区分开。

senses.title: Of a German prince-elector
senses.definition: historical use for the dignity or territory of a prince who had the right to elect the emperor
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法，指有权选举皇帝的诸侯所拥有的尊位或领地
senses.example: The electoral dignity passed to the Bavarian branch.
senses.exampleCN: 选帝侯尊位传给了巴伐利亚一支。
senses.why: The Holy Roman Empire had a small college of electors, and English borrowed the adjective for their status.
senses.whyCN: 神圣罗马帝国有一个小规模的选举人团，英语借用了这个形容词来指其地位。

senses.title: Choosing by a small body
senses.definition: extended use for a selection made by a limited group rather than a mass vote
senses.definitionCN: 引申用法，指由有限团体而非大众投票作出的选择
senses.example: The club's electoral procedure involved only nine members.
senses.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部的选举程序只涉及九名成员。
senses.why: The word keeps the idea of a defined body of choosers, which applies at any scale.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了「由一群确定的选者来选」的意思，这在任何尺度上都适用。

intro.en: Electoral is elector plus -al. Elector came into English in the mid-fifteenth century from Latin elector 'chooser', built on eligere 'to pick out'. The German electoral dignity is a sixteenth-century borrowing.
intro.cn: electoral 是 elector 加 -al。elector 于十五世纪中期从拉丁 elector「选择者」进入英语，由 eligere「挑出」构成。德意志选帝侯尊位是十六世纪的借用。

items.en: Legere meant 'to gather, pick, read', and from it came eligere 'to pick out'. The reading branch gives legible and lecture, which are not political.
items.cn: legere 意为「收集、挑选、读」，由它产生 eligere「挑出」。其中「读」的一支给出 legible 与 lecture，与政治无关。

items.en: Elector was the agent noun for a chooser, formed with -or from the past-participle stem of eligere.
items.cn: elector 是「选择者」的施事名词，由 eligere 的过去分词词干加 -or 构成。

items.en: English elector first meant one who elects or has the right of choice, and later a member of an electoral college.
items.cn: 英语 elector 先指选举者或拥有选择权的人，后指选举人团的成员。

items.en: The ending -al came from Latin -alis and marks relation, so electoral means 'of an elector' before it means 'of an election'.
items.cn: 词尾 -al 来自拉丁 -alis，标记关系，因此 electoral 先表示「选民的」，后表示「选举的」。

items.en: In the Holy Roman Empire a small college of princes held the right to elect the emperor, and English used electoral for their title and territory.
items.cn: 在神圣罗马帝国，一小群诸侯拥有选举皇帝的权利，英语用 electoral 指他们的头衔与领地。

items.en: The modern senses of systems, boundaries and fraud belong to the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, when mass electorates and seat-counting rules became central.
items.cn: 制度、边界与舞弊等现代义属于十九与二十世纪，那时大众选民与席位换算规则成为核心。

note.en: Group one holds the election family, whose members differ by ending and are often swapped; group two holds adjectives about the machinery of representation.
note.cn: 第一组是 election 词族，成员差别在词尾，常被互换；第二组是关于代表制机器的形容词。

entries.definition: A person with the right to vote, or a member of an electoral college; it names a person, not a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 指有投票权的人，或选举人团成员；它命名人，不命名性质。

entries.definition: All the voters taken together; the adjective describes them, the noun collects them.
entries.definitionCN: 指全体选民合起来；形容词描述他们，名词收集他们。

entries.definition: The process or event of voting; the adjective is what relates something to that event.
entries.definitionCN: 指投票的程序或活动；形容词表示某物与该活动相关。

entries.definition: Filled by election, or a course a student chooses; it describes a post or a subject, not the system.
entries.definitionCN: 指由选举产生的，或学生自选的课程；描述职位或科目，不描述制度。

entries.definition: Relating to a parliament; elections produce its members, but parliamentary describes the chamber's own rules and model.
entries.definitionCN: 指与议会有关的；选举产生其成员，但 parliamentary 描述议院自身的规则与模式。

entries.definition: The body of voters in a district, or the district itself; electoral describes it as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指某选区的选民群体，或该选区本身；electoral 是它的形容词说法。

entries.definition: The act or practice of casting votes; it is the plain activity, while electoral refers to the organised system.
entries.definitionCN: 指投票的行为或做法；是朴素的活动，而 electoral 指有组织的制度。

entries.definition: Relating to government and power generally; electoral is the narrower adjective for the vote alone.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与政府和权力有关的；electoral 是只就投票而言的更窄形容词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real suffix, the real root and the real institutional phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实词尾、真实词根与真实的机构搭配。

normal.en: elector plus -al 'relating to': everything that belongs to the people who choose.
normal.cn: elector 加 -al「与……有关」：一切属于那些作选择的人的事物。

normal.en: The family runs elect, election, elector, electorate, electoral and elective.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 elect、election、elector、electorate、electoral 与 elective。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the machinery: electoral system, electoral college, electoral fraud.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出机器：选举制度、选举人团、选举舞弊。

normal.en: The root eligere means 'pick out', which is what a vote does.
normal.cn: 词根 eligere 意为「挑出」，这正是投票所做的事。

normal.en: The German electoral princes show that the word is older than mass democracy.
normal.cn: 德意志选帝侯说明这个词比大众民主更老。

abstract.en: Picture a map cut into unequal squares, each square given a number larger than its size.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图被切成大小不等的方格，每格的数字都大于它的面积。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where names are crossed out and re-entered every few years.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿，每隔几年就把名字划掉再重写。

abstract.en: Picture a small room of nine people choosing for a whole city.
abstract.cn: 想象一间九个人的小屋子替整座城市作选择。

examples.en: The electoral college meets in December.
examples.cn: 选举人团在十二月开会。

examples.en: Electoral boundaries were redrawn before the vote.
examples.cn: 投票前选区边界被重新划定。

examples.en: The government promised electoral reform within a year.
examples.cn: 政府承诺一年内进行选举改革。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊-莱克-特-柔」——把「伊」人「莱克」（挑）出来，再按「特」定的「柔」软格子分票 → 选举的

root: elector + -al；elector 来自拉丁 elector「选择者」← eligere「挑出」= ex- + legere「选择」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe the same machinery from different angles: the event, the voters, the seat-counting rules, the map, the fraud, the indirect vote, the historical prince-elector and any small choosing body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从不同角度描述同一套机器：那场活动、那些选民、席位换算规则、地图、舞弊、间接投票、历史上的选帝侯、以及任何小规模的选者团体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map cut into squares, each carrying a number larger than its size.
core.cn: 核心意象：被切成方格的地图，每格的数字都大于它的面积。

branches.en: EVENT AND PEOPLE: an election and its electors are two sides of one adjective.
branches.cn: 活动与人：选举与其选民是同一形容词的两面。

branches.en: RULES AND MAP: a system needs boundaries before it can count anything.
branches.cn: 规则与地图：制度要先有边界，才能计票。

branches.en: BENDING AND LAYERING: fraud attacks the count, while indirect votes add a layer above the public.
branches.cn: 扭曲与分层：舞弊攻击计票，间接投票则在公众之上加一层。

branches.en: THE ELECTORAL PRINCE: a tiny college choosing an emperor shows the word's oldest reach.
branches.cn: 选帝侯：一个替皇帝作选择的小团体，显示这个词最老的延伸。

branches.en: THE SMALL ROOM: any limited body of choosers can use the adjective.
branches.cn: 小屋子：任何有限的选者团体都能用这个形容词。

intro.en: Electoral adds a Latin relational ending to a Latin person-noun, so the word is best read from its two pieces.
intro.cn: electoral 在拉丁人物名词上加了一个拉丁关系词尾，因此最好从两个构件来读。

latinIntro.en: Legere gives eligere and elector; -or marks the person, and -al marks the relation.
latinIntro.cn: legere 给出 eligere 与 elector；-or 标记人，-al 标记关系。

items.example: The root has two visible branches.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根有两支可见的分支。

items.example: The voters pick out one candidate.

items.meaningCN: 与选举人或选举有关的

items.example: The election drew a large turnout.

items.exampleCN: 该地区在选举上具有决定性。

definition_zh: 瀑布；跌水；瀑布般倾泻；（界面）瀑布流
definition_en: a place where a river drops over a steep edge
core_image: 河水走到岩壁尽头，整片跌下去，底部腾起白雾
scene: 山道尽头，河水从黑色岩壁上整片跌下，谷底腾起白雾。 The waterfall feeds a cold pool at the foot of the cliff.
sceneCN: 这里 waterfall 指「瀑布」（第 1 个义项：河水越过陡崖整片跌落之处）；句意为这道瀑布在崖脚汇成一汪冷水潭。

pos.zh: 瀑布；跌水；瀑布状倾泻（可数，复数 waterfalls）
瀑布式的（多用于复合术语，如瀑布模型）

derivatives.zh: waterfall + model（复合术语，无后缀）→ 像瀑布一样逐级下落的开发流程：瀑布模型
waterfall + chart（复合术语，无后缀）→ 逐项增减如跌水的图表：瀑布图
waterfall + layout（复合术语，无后缀）→ 页面元素像水帘层层排布的布局：瀑布流布局
waterfall + basin（复合术语，无后缀）→ 瀑布下方承水的潭：瀑布潭
waterfall + effect（复合术语，无后缀）→ 连锁倾泻式的影响：瀑布效应

senses.title: A natural fall of a river
senses.titleCN: 天然瀑布：河水整片跌落
senses.definition: a place where a river drops steeply over a rock edge
senses.definitionCN: 河流越过岩石陡坎整片跌落的地点
senses.example: The waterfall feeds a cold pool at the foot of the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 这道瀑布在崖脚汇成一汪冷水潭。
senses.why: water and fall are simply placed side by side: the word names water in the act of falling.
senses.whyCN: water 与 fall 直接并置：这个词命名「正在落下的水」。

senses.title: An artificial drop in a channel
senses.titleCN: 人工跌水：水利工程中的落差
senses.definition: a built step in a canal or channel where water drops to a lower level
senses.definitionCN: 渠道中人工建造、使水降到低处的落差
senses.example: A waterfall in the canal breaks the speed of the flow.
senses.exampleCN: 渠中的一处跌水减缓了流速。
senses.why: a canal repeats the natural drop in concrete, and the same word covers the built step because the shape is identical.
senses.whyCN: 运河用混凝土重复自然的落差，同样的词覆盖人工跌水，因为形状一致。

senses.title: The falling sheet of water
senses.titleCN: 瀑布水帘：跌落的那片水
senses.definition: the body of water itself as it falls, rather than the place
senses.definitionCN: 跌落中的水体本身，而非地点
senses.example: Mist rose where the waterfall struck the rocks.
senses.exampleCN: 瀑布击打岩石处腾起水雾。
senses.why: the place and the water in it are separable in thought, so the word can name the falling sheet itself.
senses.whyCN: 地点与其中的水在思维上可以分开，因此这个词能命名跌落的水帘本身。

senses.title: A waterfall as scenery
senses.titleCN: 瀑布景观：作为观赏对象
senses.definition: a waterfall viewed as a landscape feature or visitor attraction
senses.definitionCN: 被当作景观或游览对象的瀑布
senses.example: The waterfall draws thousands of visitors each summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这道瀑布每年夏天吸引数千游客。
senses.why: tourism turns the fall into an object to be visited, and the word then names the attraction rather than the drop.
senses.whyCN: 旅游把瀑布变成被参观的对象，于是这个词命名景点而非落差。

senses.title: A series of falls
senses.titleCN: 多级瀑布：一级级跌落的瀑布群
senses.definition: a succession of drops along one river, treated as a single feature
senses.definitionCN: 同一条河上连续的多级跌落，被视为一个景观
senses.example: A series of waterfalls steps down the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 一串瀑布沿山谷逐级而下。
senses.why: a staircase of drops is still one feature, so the singular word extends to a whole series.
senses.whyCN: 一串阶梯式落差仍是一个景观，因此单数词扩展到整组瀑布。

senses.title: Retreat of a waterfall by erosion
senses.titleCN: 瀑布后退：陡坎被侵蚀向上游移动
senses.definition: the upstream movement of a fall as the rock lip is eroded
senses.definitionCN: 岩石坎唇被侵蚀，使瀑布位置向上游移动
senses.example: The waterfall retreats upstream as the lip wears back.
senses.exampleCN: 坎唇被磨退，瀑布便向上游后退。
senses.why: the fall is not fixed: its lip erodes and the whole feature migrates upstream, which geology records as retreat.
senses.whyCN: 瀑布并不固定：坎唇被侵蚀，整个景观向上游迁移，地质学称之为后退。

senses.title: Anything falling in sheets
senses.titleCN: 比喻：瀑布般倾泻的事物
senses.definition: a large amount of something that seems to fall continuously
senses.definitionCN: 大量事物像水一样连续倾泻
senses.example: A waterfall of light poured through the high window.
senses.exampleCN: 一片光像瀑布一样从高窗倾泻进来。
senses.why: anything that falls in a continuous sheet shares the shape of the water, so the word becomes a metaphor for abundance.
senses.whyCN: 任何连续成片落下之物都共享水的形状，于是这个词成为「丰沛倾泻」的比喻。

senses.title: Waterfall layout or chart
senses.titleCN: 专名：瀑布流布局与瀑布图
senses.definition: a layout in which columns of uneven height flow downward, or a chart of successive gains and losses
senses.definitionCN: 高度不齐的栏目向下流动的排版，或逐项显示增减的图表
senses.example: The gallery uses a waterfall layout on small screens.
senses.exampleCN: 这个画廊在小屏幕上采用瀑布流布局。
senses.why: both computing uses keep the image of separate streams falling into place one after another.
senses.whyCN: 两种计算用法都保留了「一股股水流依次落下归位」的意象。

intro.en: Waterfall is a native English compound of water and fall. Water goes back to Old English wæter, and fall to Old English feallan 'to fall'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: waterfall 是英语本族复合词，由 water 与 fall 构成。water 上承古英语 wæter，fall 上承古英语 feallan「落下」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Wæter is the Germanic word for water, with German Wasser and Dutch water as close relatives.
items.cn: wæter 是日耳曼语的水词，德语 Wasser 与荷兰语 water 是近亲。

items.en: Feallan meant to fall or drop; the noun fall was formed from the same verb and covers both a season and an act of falling.
items.cn: feallan 意为落下、跌落；名词 fall 由同一动词构成，兼指季节与下落动作。

items.en: Water plus fall is recorded in the modern sense from the sixteenth century, when travellers described steep drops in mountain rivers.
items.cn: water 加 fall 的现代义在 16 世纪有记录，当时游记描述山间河流的陡落。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geologists explain waterfall retreat, caprock and plunge pools, fixing the technical vocabulary.
items.cn: 19 世纪地质学家解释瀑布后退、盖岩与跌水潭，固定了技术词汇。

items.en: The twentieth century adds the waterfall model in software engineering and the waterfall chart in finance; web design adds the waterfall layout.
items.cn: 20 世纪软件工程增添了 waterfall model，金融增添了 waterfall chart；网页设计又增添了 waterfall layout。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the two parts are securely documented, but the compound's earliest citation varies between references.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：两个成分均有可靠记载，但复合词的最早书证各家著录不同。

note.en: Group one holds other water compounds that are easy to swap; group two holds the words for different kinds of falling water.
note.cn: 第一组是容易混淆的其他 water 复合词；第二组是各种跌落水体的说法。

entries.definition: Birds that live on or near water; the second element is fowl, not fall.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在水上或水边的鸟；第二成分是 fowl，不是 fall。

entries.definition: The ridge between drainage basins, or the basin itself; nothing falls in it.
entries.definitionCN: 流域之间的分水岭，或指流域本身；其中并没有水落下。

entries.definition: A river or canal used for travel or transport; it names a path, not a drop.
entries.definitionCN: 用于航行或运输的河或运河；它命名路径，而非落差。

entries.definition: A wheel turned by flowing water; the second element is wheel.
entries.definitionCN: 由流水推动的轮子；第二成分是 wheel。

entries.definition: A small waterfall, or a series of them, often in a garden or a mountain stream.
entries.definitionCN: 小瀑布或一串小瀑布，常见于园林或山溪。

entries.definition: A very large or powerful waterfall; the word is also used for an eye condition.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大或有力的瀑布；该词也指一种眼病。

entries.definition: A stretch of fast, turbulent water over rocks, without a sheer fall.
entries.definitionCN: 水流湍急、越过岩石的一段河面，但没有陡直落差。

entries.definition: A waterfall or series of waterfalls, often in proper names such as Niagara Falls.
entries.definitionCN: 瀑布或瀑布群，常用于专名，如尼亚加拉瀑布。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词与固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: water + fall: the word is a picture of water falling.
normal.cn: water + fall：这个词就是「水在落」的一幅画。

normal.en: Waterfall, watershed and waterway all begin with water but end in different directions: falling, dividing, travelling.
normal.cn: waterfall、watershed、waterway 都以 water 开头，却分别落在落、分、行三个方向。

normal.en: A waterfall retreats upstream; the lip wears back and the fall moves with it.
normal.cn: 瀑布向上游后退：坎唇磨退，瀑布便跟着移动。

normal.en: The plunge pool at the foot is the basin the falling water digs.
normal.cn: 崖脚的跌水潭就是落水自己挖出的盆。

normal.en: Waterfall model, chart and layout are all visual descents, one after another.
normal.cn: 瀑布模型、瀑布图与瀑布流布局都是「一级接一级落下」的视觉比喻。

abstract.en: A waterfall is a river deciding, at one edge, to become air for a moment.
abstract.cn: 瀑布是一条河在某个边沿决定暂时变成空气。

abstract.en: Good news can arrive as a waterfall, all at once, after a long dry season.
abstract.cn: 好消息可以像瀑布一样，在漫长的旱季之后一次倾泻而下。

abstract.en: A waterfall keeps moving upstream while seeming to stand still, like a habit wearing away at its own source.
abstract.cn: 瀑布看似不动，却一直向上游移动，像一种习惯在磨蚀自己的源头。

examples.en: The waterfall drops thirty metres into the gorge.
examples.cn: 瀑布落差三十米，落入峡谷。

examples.en: Mist from the waterfall soaked their clothes.
examples.cn: 瀑布的水雾打湿了他们的衣服。

examples.en: Engineers built a waterfall to lower the canal by two metres.
examples.cn: 工程师建了一处跌水，使运河水位下降两米。

dict_mnemonic.text: water（水）+ fall（落）＝正在落下的水；天然瀑布、人工跌水、光帘比喻、瀑布流布局，都是「整片往下落」。

root: 英语本族复合词，由 water（水，古英语 wæter）与 fall（落下，古英语 feallan）直接组合。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of waterfall. The physical fall generates the rest: an artificial drop repeats it, the falling sheet is its body, scenery is how it is seen, retreat is how it ages, and the computing terms borrow its shape.
sensesIntro.cn: waterfall 的八个义项。自然瀑布衍生其余各义：人工跌水重复它，水帘是它的身体，景观是观看方式，后退是它变老的方式，而计算术语借用了它的形状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river reaches a hard edge and pours over it into mist.
core.cn: 核心意象：河流走到坚硬的边沿，整片倾泻下去，落入水雾。

branches.en: NATURAL FALLS: one drop, then a whole staircase of drops.
branches.cn: 自然瀑布：先是一处落差，再是一整段阶梯式瀑布群。

branches.en: BUILT AND AGING DROPS: an artificial step, then the natural retreat of the lip.
branches.cn: 人造与老去的落差：先是人工跌水，再是坎唇自然后退。

branches.en: THE FALLING BODY: the water itself, seen as a sheet rather than a place.
branches.cn: 跌落的水体：把水本身看作水帘，而非地点。

branches.en: THE VIEW: the fall turned into scenery and a destination.
branches.cn: 景观：瀑布被转化为风景与目的地。

branches.en: BORROWED SHAPES: light pouring like water, and interface or chart streams falling into place.
branches.cn: 借用的形状：光像水一样倾泻，界面或图表的股流依次落下归位。

intro.en: Waterfall takes no affix: it is water plus fall, and the meaning is exactly the sum of the parts.
intro.cn: waterfall 不带词缀：它是 water 加 fall，意义正是两部分之和。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Germanic and have no Latin cognates. Latin named a waterfall cataracta, borrowed from Greek kataraktes, and English later borrowed cataract; it is a different word, not a relative of waterfall.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词。拉丁语称瀑布为 cataracta，借自希腊语 kataraktes，英语后来借入 cataract；那是另一个词，与 waterfall 没有同源关系。

items.example: The fall is twenty metres high.
The waterfall is frozen in winter.

items.meaning: a software process with fixed sequential stages
items.meaningCN: 阶段固定、依次推进的软件开发流程
items.example: The team abandoned the waterfall model for shorter cycles.
items.exampleCN: 团队放弃了瀑布模型，改用更短的周期。

items.meaning: a chart showing successive increases and decreases
items.example: The waterfall chart explains the profit gap.
items.exampleCN: 瀑布图解释了利润缺口。

items.meaning: a grid whose columns flow downward at uneven heights
items.meaningCN: 各列高度不齐、向下排列的网格
items.example: The site uses a waterfall layout for photos.
items.exampleCN: 该网站用瀑布流布局展示照片。

items.meaning: the deep basin dug by falling water
items.example: Salmon rest in the plunge pool below.
items.exampleCN: 鲑鱼在下方跌水潭里歇息。

items.meaning: the hard layer that holds up a fall's lip
items.meaningCN: 托住瀑布坎唇的硬岩层
items.example: Caprock slows the retreat of the waterfall.

definition_zh: 促销的；推广宣传用的；优惠的；宣传性的
definition_en: relating to an effort that pushes a product, event or brand toward the public
core_image: 一只贴着价签的手把商品塞进顾客掌心，掌心上还印着店名
scene: 店员把印着店名的小样塞进顾客掌心，掌心还留着价签的折痕。 The promotional copy cost nothing but carried the logo on every page.
sceneCN: 店员把印着店名的小样塞进顾客掌心，掌心还留着价签的折痕；句中的这个词指「为推广而制作的」（第 2 个义项：用于宣传目的的材料或活动，而非日常售卖用品）。图中可辨识物件：小样、掌心、价签折痕、每页上的标志、柜台。

pos.zh: 促销的；推广宣传用的（多作定语）
职位晋升的（较少用）

senses.title: Relating to a sales offer
senses.definition: relating to a special offer meant to raise sales quickly
senses.definitionCN: 与旨在快速拉动销量的特殊优惠有关的
senses.example: The promotional price lasts until Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 这个促销价持续到周日。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun idea of a forward push to whatever it describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把「往前推」这一名词概念贴到它所修饰的东西上。

senses.title: Made for advertising a product or event
senses.definition: made or used for advertising a product, event or brand
senses.definitionCN: 为宣传某产品、活动或品牌而制作或使用的
senses.example: The promotional copy cost nothing but carried the logo on every page.
senses.exampleCN: 这本赠阅本不花钱，但每页都带着标志。
senses.why: Here the adjective marks purpose: the object exists in order to push something else into view.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个形容词标的是「用途」：这件东西存在，是为了把别的东西推到人眼前。

senses.title: Offered at a reduced price
senses.definition: offered at a lower price for a limited period as part of such an offer
senses.definitionCN: 作为此类活动的一部分，在限定时期内以较低价格提供
senses.example: Members buy the second ticket at the promotional rate.
senses.exampleCN: 会员可以按促销价买第二张票。
senses.why: A lower number is the cheapest kind of push: the distance to a decision shrinks.
senses.whyCN: 把数字压低是最便宜的一种「推」：到「决定买」的距离被缩短了。

senses.title: Sounding like an advertisement
senses.definition: done mainly to win approval, in a tone that sounds like advertising
senses.definitionCN: 主要为赢得赞许而做，语气听起来像广告
senses.example: His promotional remarks about the plan convinced nobody.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这个计划那些宣传腔的说法没说服任何人。
senses.why: When the push is visible in the speech itself, the adjective turns into a criticism.
senses.whyCN: 当「推」的动作在话语里露了出来，这个形容词就变成了批评。

senses.title: Given away free to be talked about
senses.definition: given away free so that people will try the thing and talk about it
senses.definitionCN: 免费送出，好让人试用并谈论它
senses.example: Bags of promotional coffee were handed out at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 车站派发了成袋的宣传用咖啡。
senses.why: A free sample buys a trial; the cost is moved from the buyer to the seller.
senses.whyCN: 免费小样买到一次试用；成本从买家一侧移到了卖家一侧。

senses.title: Relating to a rise in rank
senses.titleCN: 与职位晋升有关的（少见）
senses.definition: relating to a rise in rank or position, a rarer use
senses.definitionCN: 与职位或级别的提升有关的，较少见的用法
senses.example: The promotional ladder in this firm is unusually short.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的晋升阶梯短得出奇。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the noun survives in the adjective, though the sales sense now dominates.
senses.whyCN: 名词最古老的那个义项在这个形容词里活了下来，尽管卖货义如今占主导。

senses.title: Belonging to a fixed offer period
senses.definition: belonging to a fixed window during which the offer runs
senses.definitionCN: 属于优惠活动的固定时间窗内的
senses.example: Sales rose sharply in the promotional weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 在促销的那几周里销量猛增。
senses.why: A push has to stop, or buyers learn to wait; the adjective marks those bounded weeks.
senses.whyCN: 推的动作必须停止，否则买家会学会等待；这个形容词标出的正是那几周有边界的时段。

senses.title: Built to make a brand familiar
senses.definition: designed to build recognition of a brand rather than to sell one item that day
senses.definitionCN: 为建立品牌认知而设计，而不是为了当天卖出某件商品
senses.example: They rented a promotional stand at the trade fair.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在交易会上租了一个品牌推广展位。
senses.why: The object pushed here is a name, so the adjective serves recognition rather than an immediate sale.
senses.whyCN: 这里被推的是「一个名字」，所以这个形容词服务的是认知度，而不是当场成交。

intro.en: Promotional is promotion plus the English adjective suffix -al. Its commercial sense is only about two centuries old.
intro.cn: promotional 是 promotion 加英语形容词后缀 -al。它的商业义只有大约两百年的历史。

items.en: Movere 'to move' is the base, also behind motion, motive and emotion.
items.cn: movere「移动」是词基，也藏在 motion、motive 与 emotion 背后。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus movere gave promovere 'to move forward, to advance'.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 movere 构成 promovere「向前移、推进」。

items.en: The action noun promotio reached English as promotion, first meaning advancement in rank.
items.cn: 动作名词 promotio 以 promotion 进入英语，最初指职位的提升。

items.en: The suffix -al, from Latin -alis, turns a noun into an adjective meaning 'relating to'.
items.cn: 后缀 -al 出自拉丁 -alis，把名词变成意为「与……有关的」形容词。

items.en: As sales promotion became a trade term, the adjective promotional was applied to leaflets, prices and events that push goods.
items.cn: 随着 sales promotion 成为行业术语，形容词 promotional 被用于推动商品的那些传单、价格与活动。

items.en: The twentieth century extended the adjective to brand building, free samples and any material made for publicity.
items.cn: 二十世纪把这个形容词扩展到品牌建设、免费小样，以及任何为宣传而制作的材料。

note.en: Group one differs only in ending from words built on the same root; group two marks other kinds of commercial adjective.
note.cn: 第一组只是词尾不同，词根相同；第二组是其他类型的商业形容词。

entries.definition: The noun: the event or offer itself. The adjective describes something that serves that event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词：指那件事或那项优惠本身。形容词则描述为这件事服务的东西。

entries.definition: The passive form: someone or something that has been raised, not something that serves promotion.
entries.definitionCN: 被动形式：已被提升的人或物，而不是为推广服务的东西。

entries.definition: The person who pushes a project; it is a noun, so it cannot stand before another noun as a modifier of purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 推动项目的人；是名词，不能像形容词那样放在另一个名词前表用途。

entries.definition: A headland, from Latin mons 'mountain'. Only the opening letters resemble this family.
entries.definitionCN: 海角，出自拉丁 mons「山」。只有开头几个字母与这一族相像。

entries.definition: Relating to paid notices in media; promotional can also cover discounts, samples and stands that are not notices.
entries.definitionCN: 指媒体上的付费告示；promotional 还可涵盖折扣、小样与展位，这些都不是告示。

entries.definition: Relating to the whole selling strategy, including pricing and distribution as well as promotion.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个销售策略，除推广外还包括定价与渠道。

entries.definition: The attention gained; it often comes free, whereas promotional material is deliberately produced and paid for.
entries.definitionCN: 指获得的关注，往往免费；而 promotional 材料是特意制作并付钱的。

entries.definition: Given free as a courtesy; a free item is promotional only when it is meant to push sales or a brand.
entries.definitionCN: 出于礼遇免费给出；只有当免费品意在推动销量或品牌时才算 promotional。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real noun stem plus a real adjective suffix.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的名词词干加真实的形容词后缀。

normal.en: promotion + -al: the -al says 'relating to', so the word means 'relating to a push'.
normal.cn: promotion 加 -al：-al 表示「与……有关」，所以整个词意为「与推动有关的」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the purpose: promotional material, a promotional offer, a promotional event.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示用途：宣传材料、优惠促销、推广活动。

normal.en: The noun ladder runs promote → promotion → promotional.
normal.cn: 名词阶梯是 promote → promotion → promotional。

normal.en: The same -al suffix builds national, personal and seasonal from nouns.
normal.cn: 同一个 -al 后缀能把 national、personal、seasonal 从名词造出来。

normal.en: A free book with a logo on every page is promotional; the same book bought in a shop is not.
normal.cn: 每页都印标志的赠书是 promotional；在店里买到的同一本书则不是。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a gift into yours; the push is the adjective's whole meaning.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把礼物推进你手里；这一推就是这个形容词的全部意思。

abstract.en: The adjective never describes the seller's effort directly, only the object that carries it.
abstract.cn: 这个形容词从不直接描述卖家的努力，只描述承载那份努力的东西。

abstract.en: So promotional always answers one question: what is this object pushing?
abstract.cn: 所以 promotional 永远在回答一个问题：这件东西在推什么？

examples.en: The publisher sent promotional copies to two hundred schools.
examples.cn: 出版社向两百所学校寄送了赠阅本。

examples.en: Tickets bought with a promotional code cannot be refunded.
examples.cn: 用促销码购买的票不能退。

examples.en: Her speech sounded promotional rather than analytical.
examples.cn: 她的话听起来像宣传，而不像分析。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若-摩申-诺」——普若把货往前一摩，再挂个「诺」字牌，就成了宣传用的 → promotional 促销的

root: promotion + -al（形容词后缀）；promotion 出自拉丁 promovere「向前推进」= pro- + movere「移动」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one adjective to different carriers of a push: a price, a leaflet, a sample, a stand, a stretch of weeks or a tone of voice.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个形容词贴到不同的「推动载体」上：一个价格、一张传单、一份小样、一个展位、一段周数，或者一种语气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gift pushed into an open hand, with the giver's name printed on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份礼物被推进张开的手，礼物上印着给出者的名字。

branches.en: PRICE PUSH: a low price is the cheapest way to shorten the distance to a decision.
branches.cn: 价格推动：低价是缩短「到决定」距离的最便宜办法。

branches.en: PURPOSE: material made to advertise a thing differs from material made to make a name familiar.
branches.cn: 用途：为宣传某物而做的材料，与为让一个名字被记住而做的材料，并不相同。

branches.en: VISIBLE PUSH: when the effort shows through the words, the adjective becomes criticism.
branches.cn: 露出的推：当努力从话语里透出来，这个形容词就成了批评。

branches.en: FREE SAMPLE: the seller pays so the buyer will try.
branches.cn: 免费小样：卖家出钱，好让买家试一试。

branches.en: OLD LADDER AND SHORT WINDOW: a rank step survives as a rare use, while a bounded offer period is the modern default.
branches.cn: 旧梯子与短窗口：职级上的那一阶作为罕见用法留存，而有边界的优惠期则是现代的常态。

intro.en: The word is a noun stem plus the adjective suffix -al; both the stem and the suffix are productive.
intro.cn: 这个词是名词词干加形容词后缀 -al；词干与后缀都还能产。

latinIntro.en: The stem goes back to Latin promovere 'to move forward', built on movere 'to move'.
latinIntro.cn: 词干上溯到拉丁 promovere「向前推进」，由 movere「移动」构成。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective from a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词。
motive 与 motion 都带着它。

items.example: The motion of the ship made her ill.

definition_zh: 识字率；识字人口比例（通常以某年龄段能读写人数所占百分比表示）
definition_en: the percentage of a population, usually within a given age group, that can read and write
core_image: 一张摊开的国家统计表，纵横格子里填满百分比，旁边一支红笔把某一行圈了出来
scene: 统计局的长桌上摊着一份国别数据表，格子里的百分比排成一片。 The literacy rate for young women doubled in twenty years.
sceneCN: 这里指「能读写人口所占的百分比」（第 1 个义项：衡量识字普及程度的比例指标）；句意为青年女性的识字率在二十年内翻了一番。可辨识物件：数据表、百分比、红笔、长桌。

pos.zh: 识字率（可数）

senses.title: The share of adults who can read
senses.titleCN: 成年人口中能读写的比例
senses.definition: the percentage of people above a stated age who can read and write a simple text
senses.definitionCN: 超过某一年龄的人口中，能读懂并写出浅近文字的百分比
senses.example: The adult literacy rate in the district passed ninety percent last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年该区的成人识字率超过了百分之九十。
senses.why: the phrase simply puts a measured ability next to a word for a computed proportion.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语只是把一项被测量的能力，与一个表计算比例的词并置。

senses.title: A rate for the young
senses.titleCN: 特定青年年龄段的识字比例
senses.definition: a figure limited to an age band such as fifteen to twenty-four, used to judge schools
senses.definitionCN: 限定在如十五至二十四岁年龄段、用于评估学校成效的数字
senses.example: The youth literacy rate is the clearest sign of what schooling achieved.
senses.exampleCN: 青年识字率是学校教育成效最清楚的标志。
senses.why: limiting the age band makes the number answer a specific question about recent schooling.
senses.whyCN: 限定年龄段，能让这个数字回答关于近期学校教育的具体问题。

senses.title: A national statistic for reports
senses.titleCN: 用于报告的国家统计数字
senses.definition: an official figure a state reports to international bodies
senses.definitionCN: 国家向国际机构报告的一官方数字
senses.example: Each country submits its literacy rate to the agency every year.
senses.exampleCN: 每个国家每年向该机构提交本国的识字率。
senses.why: a single comparable figure is what international reporting requires, so the phrase became official language.
senses.whyCN: 国际报告需要的正是一个可比较的数字，这个短语因此成为官方语言。

senses.title: A measure of the gender gap
senses.definition: a pair of figures compared between women and men to show inequality
senses.definitionCN: 把女性与男性数字并列比较以显示不平等的指标
senses.example: The gender gap in the literacy rate narrowed over two decades.
senses.exampleCN: 识字率中的性别差距在二十年间缩小了。
senses.why: a single rate can be split by sex, and the comparison is what makes inequality visible.
senses.whyCN: 同一个比率可以按性别拆分，而正是这种比较让不平等变得可见。

senses.title: A way to compare regions
senses.titleCN: 用于比较地区差异的尺度
senses.definition: a single number that lets provinces, cities or districts be ranked against each other
senses.definitionCN: 用一个数字让各省、市或区相互比较排序
senses.example: The literacy rate in the mountain counties lagged behind the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 山区各县的识字率落后于沿海。
senses.why: one figure can be set beside another, which turns a description into a ranking.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字能与另一个并排放置，于是描述变成了排序。

senses.title: A development indicator
senses.definition: one of the figures used to track progress in education and poverty reduction
senses.definitionCN: 用于追踪教育与减贫进展的数字之一
senses.example: Donors watched the literacy rate as one sign of reform.
senses.exampleCN: 捐助方把识字率作为改革迹象之一来观察。
senses.why: aid decisions needed a small set of numbers, and this one entered the standard list.
senses.whyCN: 援助决策需要一小组数字，而这个数字进入了标准清单。

senses.title: A census-derived figure
senses.titleCN: 由人口普查得出的数字
senses.definition: a number produced by asking people in a census whether they can read
senses.definitionCN: 通过普查询问人们能否读写而得出的数字
senses.example: Census data put the literacy rate slightly above the survey estimate.
senses.exampleCN: 普查数据使识字率略高于抽样调查的估计。
senses.why: the number has to come from somewhere, and a census is the largest source that asks everyone.
senses.whyCN: 这个数字必须有来源，而普查是询问所有人的最大来源。

senses.title: A policy target
senses.definition: a level that a government or agency commits itself to reach by a stated date
senses.definitionCN: 政府或机构承诺在指定日期前达到的水平
senses.example: The plan set a literacy rate target of ninety-five percent by the year two thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 该计划把二零零零年前的识字率目标定为百分之九十五。
senses.why: a measured figure becomes a target as soon as a government promises to move it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦政府承诺推动这个数字，测量值就成了目标。

intro.en: Literacy rate joins literacy, from Latin littera 'letter', and rate, from Latin rata pars 'a fixed portion' and reri 'to reckon'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语由表「读写能力」与表「比率」的两个名词组合：前者出自拉丁 littera「字母」，后者出自拉丁 rata pars「定额部分」与 reri「计算」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Littera meant a letter of the alphabet; with the adjective litteratus it gave the modern word for being able to read.
items.cn: littera 指字母；与形容词 litteratus 一起，构成现代表「能读写」的词。

items.en: Rata pars meant 'a reckoned or fixed portion', from the participle of reri 'to reckon, think'.
items.cn: rata pars 意为「计算过的、定额的部分」，出自 reri「计算、思考」的分词。

items.en: English rate, borrowed through French, first named a fixed charge or proportion and later any measured ratio.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入「比率」一词，先指固定费用或比例，后指任何被测量的比率。

items.en: The phrase appeared with mass statistics in the twentieth century, when states needed one number for reading ability.
items.cn: 这个短语随二十世纪的大众统计出现，当时国家需要用一个数字表示读写能力。

items.en: International agencies standardized age bands and definitions, making the phrase a comparable indicator.
items.cn: 国际机构统一了年龄段与定义，使这个短语成为可比较的指标。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the letter-word is unknown, and the first use of the exact phrase in an official report is not dated with certainty.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个表「字母」的词在拉丁语之前的来源不明，这个确切短语首次出现在官方报告中的时间亦无法确证。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike phrases built from the same two nouns; group two holds other educational proportions that are often mistaken for it.
note.cn: 第一组是由同两个名词构成的形近短语；第二组是常被误当作它的其他教育比例。

entries.definition: The ability itself; the full phrase adds a computed proportion to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指能力本身；完整短语在此基础上加了计算出的比例。

entries.definition: Any measured proportion or charge; it says nothing about reading.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何被测量的比例或费率，与读写无关。

entries.definition: The percentage who cannot read; the two figures usually sum to the whole population.
entries.definitionCN: 指不能读写的百分比，两个数字通常合成全体人口。

entries.definition: How well people read rather than what share can read, so it is a quality measure.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们读得多好，而非能读的人占多少，属质量尺度。

entries.definition: The share of children registered in school; being enrolled does not prove being literate.
entries.definitionCN: 指注册入学的儿童比例；入学并不等于识字。

entries.definition: The share who finish a level of schooling; it measures persistence, not reading.
entries.definitionCN: 指完成某一学段的比例，衡量的是坚持度而非阅读能力。

entries.definition: The comparable percentage for basic number skills, built on the same pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 指基本数字能力的对应百分比，按同一模式构成。

entries.definition: A composite score mixing years of school and qualifications, unlike the single figure of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指混合了受教育年限与学历的综合得分，不同于该短语的单一数字。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Half the phrase is an ability and half is a computed proportion, so it always needs a population behind it.
normal.cn: 短语一半是能力，一半是算出的比例，因此它背后总要有一个人群。

normal.en: Fixed phrases attach an age band: adult literacy rate, youth literacy rate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配加上年龄段：成人识字率、青年识字率。

normal.en: The complement is the illiteracy rate, and the two usually add up to the whole.
normal.cn: 它的互补项是文盲率，两者通常加成全体的整体。

normal.en: The second noun is the same one used in interest rate and birth rate.
normal.cn: 第二个名词也用于利率与出生率。

normal.en: The family runs literacy, literate, illiteracy, enrollment rate, completion rate.
normal.cn: 同族包括「读写能力」「识字的」「文盲状态」「入学率」「完成率」。

abstract.en: Picture a long table of percentages with one row circled in red.
abstract.cn: 想象一张满是百分比的长表，其中一行被红笔圈出。

abstract.en: Picture a hundred people in a hall, and a hand counting those who can sign their names.
abstract.cn: 想象大厅里有一百人，一只手在数能签自己名字的人。

abstract.en: Picture two staircases side by side, one for women and one for men, measured at the same step.
abstract.cn: 想象并排的两道楼梯，一道为女性、一道为男性，在同一级台阶上测量。

examples.en: The national literacy rate rose from sixty to eighty percent in a generation.
examples.cn: 全国识字率在一代人之内从六成升到八成。

examples.en: Agencies compare literacy rates only when the age bands match.
examples.cn: 只有当年龄段一致时，各机构才会比较识字率。

examples.en: The province set a literacy rate target for rural women.
examples.cn: 该省为农村女性设定了识字率目标。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里特乐西」加「瑞特」——认得字的人按比例排成一列，就是识字率。

root: literacy 出自拉丁 littera「字母」及其形容词 litteratus「识字的」；rate 经法语出自拉丁 rata pars「定额部分」与 reri「计算」，本指固定比例，后泛指被测量的比率。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all turn one ability into a number: a share of adults, a band of youth, a national report, a gender comparison, a regional ranking, a development indicator, a census product and finally a target to reach.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把这同一种能力变成一个数字：成人比例、青年年龄段、国家报告、性别比较、地区排序、发展指标、普查产物，最后是一个要达成的目标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide table of percentages with one row circled in red.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张铺开的百分比大表，其中一行被红笔圈出。

branches.en: THE FIRST NUMBER: the share of adults who can read is the standard form.
branches.cn: 第一个数字：能读写的成人比例是标准形态。

branches.en: AGE BANDS: narrowing the figure to the young shows what schools achieved.
branches.cn: 年龄段：把数字收窄到青年，可看出学校的成效。

branches.en: REPORTED AND COUNTED: official submissions and census returns feed the figure.
branches.cn: 上报与计数：官方提交与普查回报为这个数字提供数据。

branches.en: COMPARISONS: the same number ranks men against women and one region against another.
branches.cn: 比较：同一个数字可把男女、把一个地区与另一个地区排出高低。

branches.en: FROM SIGN TO GOAL: a development indicator also becomes a level to reach by a date.
branches.cn: 从迹象到目标：发展指标也会变成须在某日期前达到的水平。

intro.en: The phrase is two nouns, one for an ability and one for a computed proportion, each with a productive Latin core.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个名词构成，一个表能力，一个表计算出的比例，各自都有一个能产的拉丁内核。

latinIntro.en: Latin littera and litteratus supply the reading family; Latin rata and reri supply the family of reckoning and ratio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 littera 与 litteratus 提供「读写」一族；拉丁 rata 与 reri 提供「计算与比率」一族。

items.example: The root names what a reader must first learn.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指读者最先要学的东西。

items.meaning: the ability to read and write
items.exampleCN: 读写能力是被测量的，而非假定的。

items.example: The rate is stated as a percentage.
items.exampleCN: 这个比率以百分比表示。

items.example: The ratio of readers to non-readers was two to one.
items.exampleCN: 能读者与不能读者之比为二比一。

items.structure: Latin ratio carried into French and English
items.example: The same root that counts also thinks.
items.exampleCN: 同一个表示「计算」的词根也用于「思考」。

items.example: A literate adult counts once in the numerator.
items.exampleCN: 一个识字成人计入分子一次。

items.example: The two rates usually sum to the whole.
items.exampleCN: 两个比率通常加成全体的整体。

items.example: Enrollment can rise before literacy does.
items.exampleCN: 入学率可能先于识字率上升。
